meta.title: MCAN Daily Islamic Content Library
meta.description: Daily Islamic content for Muslim Corps Members — 52 weeks of Hadith, Azkar, Tawheed, Fiqh, Jumuah, Companion Stories and Quranic Stories
meta.admin_instructions: To add new content: append new week objects following the same schema. Each day contains an array of content objects. Increment week number and use the id format w{N}-{day}-{001}. All content must be sourced from authorized Sunni scholar books.
sources_used: Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir
Siyar Alam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi
Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli
Kitab at-Tawheed by Ibn Abd al-Wahhab
Jami al-Ulum wal-Hikam by Ibn Rajab
Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
Sharh al-Aqeedah al-Tahawiyyah by Ibn Abi al-Izz

monday.title: Hadith on Intentions
monday.arabic_text: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
monday.english_text: Indeed, actions are judged by intentions, and every person will have only what they intended.
monday.transliteration: Innamal a'maalu binniyyaat, wa innamaa likulli imri'in maa nawaa.
monday.chain_of_narration: Umar ibn al-Khattab → Alqamah ibn Waqqas → Muhammad ibn Ibrahim at-Taymi → Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari → Imam Malik / Sufyan ath-Thawri
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (1) and Sahih Muslim (1907).
monday.lesson: Every action we perform — whether prayer, work, study, or da'wah — is weighed by its intention. If your service year is dedicated to pleasing Allah, every moment of your NYSC becomes an act of worship. Renew your intention daily.
monday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Vol. 1, Book 1, Hadith 1; Sahih Muslim, Book of Leadership, Hadith 1907

monday.title: Hadith on Honesty
monday.arabic_text: عَلَيْكُمْ بِالصِّدْقِ، فَإِنَّ الصِّدْقَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْبِرِّ، وَإِنَّ الْبِرَّ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
monday.english_text: You must be truthful, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise.
monday.transliteration: Alaykum bis-sidq, fa-innas-sidqa yahdee ilal-birr, wa innal-birra yahdee ilal-jannah.
monday.chain_of_narration: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud → Abu Wa'il → Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir → Shu'bah
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (6094) and Sahih Muslim (2607).
monday.lesson: As a corps member representing your faith, your honesty in small matters — from attendance registers to community reports — is an act of worship. Islam elevates honesty as a path to Jannah itself.
monday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6094; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2607

tuesday.title: Morning Dhikr — SubhanAllah wa bihamdihi
tuesday.arabic_text: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
tuesday.english_text: Glory be to Allah and all praise is due to Him.
tuesday.transliteration: SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi.
tuesday.benefits: Whoever says this 100 times in the morning and evening will have all their sins forgiven, even if they are as abundant as the foam of the sea. This dhikr is light on the tongue but heavy on the Scale.
tuesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6405; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2691. From Riyad as-Salihin by Imam an-Nawawi.

tuesday.title: Dhikr After Salah — Tasbeeh, Tahmeed, Takbeer
tuesday.arabic_text: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ (٣٣) الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ (٣٣) اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ (٣٣) لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
tuesday.english_text: Glory be to Allah (33 times). Praise be to Allah (33 times). Allah is the Greatest (33 times). There is no god but Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belongs all dominion and all praise, and He has power over all things.
tuesday.transliteration: SubhanAllah (33x). Alhamdulillah (33x). Allahu Akbar (33x). La ilaha illAllahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, lahul mulku wa lahul hamdu wa Huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadeer.
tuesday.benefits: The Prophet said: 'Whoever glorifies Allah 33 times after every prayer, praises Him 33 times, and declares His greatness 33 times... his sins will be forgiven even if they are as abundant as the foam of the sea.' These 99 dhikrs form the most rewarding post-Salah remembrance.
tuesday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 597. Commentary from Sharh Sahih Muslim by Imam an-Nawawi.

wednesday.title: Tawheed al-Uluhiyyah — Singling Out Allah in Worship
wednesday.arabic_text: وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ
wednesday.english_text: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. (Quran 51:56)
wednesday.lesson: The core of Tawheed al-Uluhiyyah is directing all acts of worship — prayer, supplication, sacrifice, love, fear, and hope — solely to Allah. In a world of social pressures, peer worship of status and wealth, the corps member must anchor every ambition in this truth: we were created to worship Allah alone.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Real-life scenario: A Muslim corps member is offered a bribe to falsify community development records. The fear of Allah (and not just the law) is what truly deters the believer. This is an act of Tawheed — fearing Allah above all others.

Q: Is it worship if I perform Salah while being distracted by work?
A: The obligation is fulfilled, but the reward is diminished. Khushu' (concentration) in Salah is from the perfection of worship. Scholars recommend saying 'Allahu Akbar' and imagining this is your last prayer.
wednesday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah adh-Dhariyat 51:56; Kitab at-Tawheed by Shaykh Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab

wednesday.title: Tawheed ar-Rububiyyah — Allah's Lordship Over All Creation
wednesday.arabic_text: رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فَاعْبُدْهُ وَاصْطَبِرْ لِعِبَادَتِهِ
wednesday.english_text: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them — so worship Him and be steadfast in His worship. (Quran 19:65)
wednesday.lesson: Believing that Allah alone creates, sustains, and controls the universe is called Tawheed ar-Rububiyyah. Even the mushrikeen of Makkah believed this — yet they still associated partners with Allah in worship. So believing Allah is Lord is necessary but not sufficient; we must also worship Him alone.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: If I believe in Allah, why do I still need to avoid consulting fortune-tellers?
A: Consulting fortune-tellers is Shirk in Tawheed al-Uluhiyyah — you are directing worship (trust/reliance) to other than Allah. The Prophet said: 'Whoever visits a fortune-teller and believes what he says has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad.' (Abu Dawud 3904)
wednesday.source: Tafsir as-Sa'di, Surah Maryam 19:65; Explanation of the Three Fundamental Principles by Shaykh Ibn al-'Uthaymeen

thursday.title: Fiqh of Salat al-Jama'ah — Congregational Prayer
thursday.arabic_text: صَلَاةُ الْجَمَاعَةِ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ صَلَاةِ الْفَذِّ بِسَبْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ دَرَجَةً
thursday.english_text: Congregational prayer is twenty-seven degrees superior to individual prayer.
thursday.lesson: Scholars of the four madhabs agree that congregational prayer is at minimum Sunnah Mu'akkadah (strongly confirmed Sunnah), with the Hanbali madhab holding it to be fard (obligatory). As a corps member living at your PPA, you should actively seek mosques nearby and organize jama'ah with fellow Muslim corps members even if only two of you are present.
thursday.extra_notes:
Ruling on missing Jumu'ah: Missing three consecutive Jumu'ah prayers without excuse causes the heart to be sealed (Tirmidhi, 500). If your CDS or official assignment clashes with Jumu'ah, you must request accommodation from your supervisor. MCAN can assist with official letters.

Jama'ah for women: Congregational prayer is not obligatory for women, though they may attend the masjid. Their prayer at home is equally valid.
thursday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 645; Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq; Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli

thursday.title: Fiqh of Zakah — Who Must Pay and How
thursday.arabic_text: وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ
thursday.english_text: And establish prayer and give Zakah. (Quran 2:110)
thursday.lesson: Zakah becomes obligatory when one possesses wealth that reaches the nisab (threshold) and one full lunar year (hawl) passes while maintaining it. The nisab for gold is 85 grams; for silver, 595 grams. As corps members receiving an allowance, Zakah is generally not due on monthly salary if it does not reach the nisab and hawl simultaneously — but it is praiseworthy to give Sadaqah (voluntary charity) regularly.
thursday.extra_notes:
Common question: Do I pay Zakah on my NYSC allowance?
Answer: Your monthly stipend is consumed before a year passes, so the hawl condition is not met. However, if you save and the savings remain above nisab for a full lunar year, Zakah becomes due on those savings at 2.5%.
thursday.source: Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh, Vol. 3, Wahbah az-Zuhayli; Sharh al-Mumti' by Shaykh Ibn al-'Uthaymeen

friday.title: Jumu'ah Rites — Preparation and Sunnah Acts
friday.arabic_text: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَاةِ مِن يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فَاسْعَوْا إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَذَرُوا الْبَيْعَ
friday.english_text: O you who have believed, when the call to prayer is made on the day of Jumu'ah, proceed immediately to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. (Quran 62:9)
friday.lesson: Friday is the 'Sayyid al-Ayyam' (master of all days). Among the Sunnah acts: perform ghusl (bath), wear clean/best clothes, use miswak, apply perfume (men only), read Surah al-Kahf, send abundant salawat (prayers) upon the Prophet, make du'a especially in the last hour before Maghrib, go early to the masjid, and listen attentively to the khutbah.
friday.extra_notes: The hidden hour (Sa'ah al-Khafiyyah): The Prophet mentioned a hidden hour on Friday when du'a is accepted. Most scholars identify it as the last hour before Maghrib. Make it a habit to make sincere du'a at this time every Friday.
friday.source: Quran 62:9; Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 881; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on the Virtues of Friday

friday.title: Friday Azkar — Salawat upon the Prophet
friday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
friday.english_text: O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.
friday.transliteration: Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa 'ala aali Muhammadin, kamaa sallayta 'ala Ibraheema wa 'ala aali Ibraheema, innaka Hameedun Majeed.
friday.benefits: The Prophet said: 'Whoever sends salawat upon me once, Allah will send ten blessings upon him, erase ten of his sins, and raise him ten degrees.' (Sahih Muslim). On Friday, increase this dhikr abundantly.
friday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3370; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 406; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

saturday.title: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA) — The First Believer
saturday.arabic_text: خَيْرُ نِسَائِهَا مَرْيَمُ بِنْتُ عِمْرَانَ، وَخَيْرُ نِسَائِهَا خَدِيجَةُ بِنْتُ خُوَيْلِدٍ
saturday.english_text: The best of its women was Maryam daughter of Imran, and the best of its women was Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid. (Sahih Muslim)
saturday.lesson:
Khadijah (RA) was the first to embrace Islam, the first to believe in the Prophet when the revelation came, and she spent her entire wealth in the service of Islam. When the Prophet returned trembling from the Cave of Hira, it was her words of comfort that steadied him. She died before the hijrah, yet her status is among the highest in Jannah.

Lesson for corps members: True support for Islam does not require a position. Khadijah's contribution was her belief, her wealth, and her emotional support. You can serve Islam through your finances, your comfort to others, and your unwavering faith.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3820; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2430; As-Seerah an-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham

saturday.title: Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) — The Voice of Tawheed
saturday.arabic_text: أَحَدٌ أَحَدٌ
saturday.english_text: One (Allah). One (Allah).
saturday.lesson:
Bilal was an Abyssinian slave who became one of the most beloved companions of the Prophet. When tortured by his master Umayyah ibn Khalaf for accepting Islam — laid on burning sand with rocks on his chest — his only response was 'Ahad! Ahad!' Abu Bakr (RA) purchased and freed him. The Prophet later made him the first Mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer) of Islam.

Lesson: Your faith may be tested in your place of posting — through peer pressure, mockery, or difficulty. Like Bilal, hold firm to Tawheed regardless of social pressure. Your 'Ahad' in the face of temptation is the greatest victory.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3754; Usud al-Ghabah by Ibn al-Athir; As-Seerah an-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: The Story of Yusuf (AS) — Patience and Purity
sunday.arabic_text: إِنَّهُ مَن يَتَّقِ وَيَصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
sunday.english_text: Indeed, whoever fears Allah and is patient — then indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good. (Quran 12:90)
sunday.lesson:
Yusuf (AS) was thrown into a well by his brothers, sold into slavery, falsely accused and imprisoned — yet at every stage, he maintained his taqwa and patience. Allah's plan unfolded perfectly and he became the Aziz of Egypt.

For corps members away from home, in unfamiliar states: your displacement mirrors in a small way the trials of Yusuf (AS). Use this year to build your character, resist temptation like he did, and trust that Allah's plan for you is better than any you could devise.
sunday.source: Quran, Surah Yusuf 12:1-101; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Yusuf; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: The People of the Cave — Ahl al-Kahf
sunday.arabic_text: إِنَّهُمْ فِتْيَةٌ آمَنُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ وَزِدْنَاهُمْ هُدًى
sunday.english_text: Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance. (Quran 18:13)
sunday.lesson:
A group of young men in a tyrannical society chose faith over comfort, fleeing to a cave rather than renouncing their belief in Allah. Allah caused them to sleep for 309 years and made their story a sign for all of humanity.

You are the 'youth who believed.' The Quran celebrates young people who choose Allah over conformity. Reading Surah al-Kahf every Friday protects from the Dajjal and is a reminder that sincere faith in youth is the greatest honor.
sunday.source: Quran 18:9-26; Tafsir as-Sa'di, Surah al-Kahf; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 809 on virtues of Surah al-Kahf

monday.title: Hadith on the Best of People
monday.english_text: The best of people are those who are most beneficial to people.
monday.chain_of_narration: Jabir ibn Abdullah → narrated through multiple chains including al-Hakim
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat by al-Tabarani and authenticated by al-Albani in Silsilah as-Sahihah (426).
monday.lesson: The NYSC programme calls corps members to serve communities. This hadith reminds us that community service is not merely civic duty — it is the essence of being among Allah's best servants. Make your community development project a sincere act of worship.
monday.source: Al-Mu'jam al-Awsat by al-Tabarani; Silsilah as-Sahihah by al-Albani, Hadith 426

monday.title: Hadith on Gentleness
monday.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ، وَيُعْطِي عَلَى الرِّفْقِ مَا لَا يُعْطِي عَلَى الْعُنْفِ
monday.english_text: Verily, Allah is gentle and loves gentleness. He grants for gentleness what He does not grant for harshness.
monday.transliteration: Innallaha rafeequn yuhibbur-rifq, wa yu'ti 'alar-rifqi ma la yu'ti 'alal-'unf.
monday.chain_of_narration: Aisha (RA) → Urwah ibn az-Zubayr → Hisham ibn Urwah → several transmitters
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her). Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (6927) and Sahih Muslim (2593).
monday.lesson: Whether teaching in a school, organizing CDS events, or navigating tensions among corps members of different backgrounds — gentleness is the Islamic approach. It achieves more than force ever can.
monday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6927; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2593

tuesday.title: Morning Dhikr — Hasbiyallahu la ilaha illa Huwa
tuesday.arabic_text: حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَهُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ
tuesday.english_text: Allah is sufficient for me. There is no god but Him. I have put my trust in Him, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.
tuesday.transliteration: Hasbiyallahu la ilaha illa Huwa, 'alayhi tawakkaltu wa Huwa Rabbul-'Arshil-'Azeem.
tuesday.benefits: Whoever recites this 7 times morning and evening, Allah will suffice him in whatever concerns him in this world and the next. This dhikr builds tawakkul (reliance on Allah) — a critical quality for a corps member navigating uncertain postings and environments.
tuesday.source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 5081; Authenticated in Silsilah as-Sahihah by al-Albani; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

tuesday.title: Evening Dhikr — Ayat al-Kursi
tuesday.arabic_text: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ
tuesday.english_text: Allah! There is no god but He — the Living, the Eternal. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. (Quran 2:255)
tuesday.transliteration: Allahu la ilaha illa Huwal-Hayyul-Qayyum, la ta'khudhuhu sinatun wa la nawm...
tuesday.benefits: Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after each obligatory prayer, nothing will prevent them from entering Jannah except death. Reciting it before sleeping brings the protection of Allah throughout the night. A corps member in an unfamiliar environment should not sleep without this dhikr.
tuesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari (Hadith on virtues of Ayat al-Kursi); Sunan an-Nasa'i, Hadith 9928; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

wednesday.title: Tawheed al-Asma was-Sifat — Allah's Names and Attributes
wednesday.english_text: And to Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them. (Quran 7:180)
wednesday.lesson: The third category of Tawheed is affirming Allah's names and attributes as they appear in the Quran and authentic Sunnah — without distortion, denial, resemblance to creation, or asking 'how.' Allah is Al-'Alim (All-Knowing), Al-Qadir (All-Powerful), As-Sami' (All-Hearing). Understanding these names transforms worship from ritual to relationship.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Real-life scenario: A corps member is posting falsified data in their CDS report, thinking no one will find out. Knowing that Allah is Al-Khabir (All-Aware of hidden things) should be a deterrent far stronger than any supervisor's scrutiny.

Q: Can we say Allah 'literally' sits on the Throne?
A: Ahlus-Sunnah affirm that Allah is above His Throne (Quran 20:5) in a manner that befits His Majesty, without asking 'how.' We affirm the attribute without likening it to creation. This is the way of the Salaf.
wednesday.source: Kitab at-Tawheed by Shaykh Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab; Sharh al-Aqeedah al-Wasitiyyah by Shaykh Ibn al-'Uthaymeen

wednesday.title: Shirk al-Asghar — Minor Polytheism: Showing Off (Riya')
wednesday.arabic_text: إِنَّ أَخْوَفَ مَا أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمُ الشِّرْكُ الْأَصْغَرُ قَالُوا وَمَا الشِّرْكُ الْأَصْغَرُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ الرِّيَاءُ
wednesday.english_text: The thing I fear most for you is minor shirk. They asked: What is minor shirk, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Showing off (Riya').
wednesday.lesson: Riya' is performing acts of worship to be seen or praised by people rather than for Allah's sake. It does not make one a disbeliever but nullifies the act of worship it corrupts. The Prophet feared it for his companions more than he feared outright shirk — because it is subtle. Check your intention before every prayer, every charitable act, every Islamic post on social media.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: If I post my Islamic knowledge on social media and people praise me, is that riya'?
A: Scholars distinguish between intending praise from the outset (riya') and receiving unexpected praise afterward. If you post sincerely for da'wah and people praise you, the praise does not nullify your act. But if you craft the post to impress others, that is riya'. Renew your intention constantly.
wednesday.source: Musnad Ahmad, Hadith 23630; Classified as Sahih by al-Albani; Tafsir Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali in Jami' al-Ulum wal-Hikam

thursday.title: Fiqh of Wudu — Conditions, Pillars and Nullifiers
thursday.arabic_text: لَا تُقْبَلُ صَلَاةٌ بِغَيْرِ طَهُورٍ
thursday.english_text: No prayer is accepted without purification.
thursday.lesson: Wudu (ablution) is a condition for the validity of Salah. Its pillars include: intention, washing the face, washing the arms to the elbows, wiping the head, and washing the feet to the ankles. Among the nullifiers are: passing wind, answering the call of nature, deep sleep, loss of consciousness, and eating camel meat (Hanbali opinion). As a corps member, knowing when your wudu is broken prevents praying in an invalid state.
thursday.extra_notes:
Common question: Does touching the opposite gender break wudu?
Answer: The madhabs differ. Hanafi and Hanbali: No, unless accompanied by desire. Shafi'i: Yes, mere touching breaks it (unless mahram). Maliki: Only with desire. Choose a madhab and follow it consistently. The safest position when in doubt is to renew wudu.

Practical note: Masah (wiping) over leather socks (khuffayn) is valid for 24 hours for a resident and 72 hours for a traveler — useful for corps members in the field.
thursday.source: Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq, Vol. 1; Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli; Bidayat al-Mujtahid by Ibn Rushd

thursday.title: Fiqh of Tayammum — Dry Ablution When Water is Absent
thursday.arabic_text: فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا مَاءً فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا فَامْسَحُوا بِوُجُوهِكُمْ وَأَيْدِيكُمْ
thursday.english_text: And if you find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands. (Quran 4:43)
thursday.lesson: Tayammum is permitted when: water is unavailable, its use would harm you due to illness, or you fear missing the prayer time before accessing water. It is performed by striking clean earth with the palms once, then wiping the face and hands. This dispensation demonstrates Islam's ease (yusr). Corps members on field trips, remote postings, or in water-scarce LGAs should know this ruling.
thursday.extra_notes:
Q: Can I use a stone wall or dusty surface for tayammum?
A: Yes, according to the majority of scholars — any clean earth surface (sa'id) qualifies. The Hanafi school requires actual soil or dust. The Maliki and Hanbali schools allow stones and surfaces with dust on them.

Q: Does tayammum remain valid when water becomes available?
A: No. Once you gain access to water, tayammum is immediately nullified and wudu must be performed before the next prayer.
thursday.source: Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq, Vol. 1; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah; Al-Fiqh 'ala al-Madhahib al-Arba'ah by al-Jaziri

friday.title: The Virtues of Surah al-Kahf on Friday
friday.arabic_text: مَنْ قَرَأَ سُورَةَ الْكَهْفِ فِي يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ أَضَاءَ لَهُ مِنَ النُّورِ مَا بَيْنَ الْجُمُعَتَيْنِ
friday.english_text: Whoever recites Surah al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for him between the two Fridays.
friday.lesson: Surah al-Kahf contains four great stories: the People of the Cave (trial of faith), the owner of two gardens (trial of wealth), Musa and al-Khidr (trial of knowledge), and Dhul-Qarnayn (trial of power). Reciting this surah every Friday illuminates the heart against the four greatest trials of life — all of which a young Muslim corps member may face in a single service year.
friday.extra_notes:
Best time to recite: From sunset on Thursday through the day of Friday (scholars differ on exact window). Some say it is best to recite it at night on Thursday, others say during the day on Friday before Asr. Either is valid.

Tip: If you cannot recite the whole surah, at minimum recite the first and last ten verses. The Prophet said the first ten verses protect from Dajjal. (Sahih Muslim, Hadith 809)
friday.source: Sunan al-Bayhaqi; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak; authenticated in Silsilah as-Sahihah by al-Albani (2651)

friday.title: Friday Azkar — Du'a of the Last Hour
friday.arabic_text: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
friday.english_text: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. (Quran 2:201)
friday.transliteration: Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-naar.
friday.benefits: This is the most comprehensive du'a in the Quran. Anas ibn Malik (RA) said the Prophet frequently made this supplication. On Friday, in the final hour before Maghrib, this du'a carries immense weight. It asks for goodness in both worlds — the perfect du'a for a corps member beginning their life journey.
friday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 4522; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2690; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 2:201

saturday.title: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA) — The Truthful One
saturday.arabic_text: مَا سَبَقَكُمْ أَبُو بَكْرٍ بِكَثْرَةِ صَلَاةٍ وَلَا صِيَامٍ وَلَكِنْ بِشَيْءٍ وَقَرَ فِي قَلْبِهِ
saturday.english_text: Abu Bakr did not surpass you by excessive fasting or prayer, but by something that settled in his heart.
saturday.lesson:
Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was the closest companion of the Prophet, the first adult male Muslim, and the man who never doubted the Isra' wal-Mi'raj for a single moment — earning the title 'as-Siddiq' (the Truthful). When the Prophet died and companions were in shock, it was Abu Bakr who steadied the Ummah: 'Whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad is dead. Whoever worshipped Allah, Allah is Ever-Living and never dies.'

Lesson: The mark of the greatest Muslims is not the quantity of their deeds but the quality of their heart. Sincerity, firm belief, and love for Allah and His Messenger — these were Abu Bakr's secrets. Cultivate your heart this service year.
saturday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 3656; Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3668; As-Seerah an-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham

saturday.title: Salman al-Farisi (RA) — The Seeker Who Crossed the World
saturday.arabic_text: سَلْمَانُ مِنَّا أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ
saturday.english_text: Salman is from us, the People of the House (of the Prophet).
saturday.lesson:
Salman al-Farisi was born a Zoroastrian in Persia. He sought truth, traveling from Persia to Syria, following Christian monks, then to the Arabian Peninsula — all in search of the final Prophet. Enslaved along the way, he finally met the Prophet Muhammad in Madinah and recognized him by the seal of prophethood. The Prophet called him 'from the people of the house.'

Lesson: The pursuit of truth transcends all barriers — ethnicity, geography, social class. Salman's story tells the Muslim corps member that no posting is too remote, no obstacle too great, when one is sincerely seeking Allah. Your service year, even in a distant state, may be the very experience that deepens your faith.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3991 (mention in Khandaq); Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar; As-Seerah an-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: Ibrahim (AS) — The Breaking of Idols
sunday.arabic_text: وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّنِي بَرَاءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ
sunday.english_text: And mention when Ibrahim said to his father and his people: Indeed, I am free of what you worship. (Quran 43:26)
sunday.lesson:
Ibrahim (AS) grew up in a family and society of idol-worshippers, yet he questioned, reasoned, and ultimately broke the idols in the temple to make his people think. He was cast into a blazing fire rather than compromise his Tawheed — and Allah commanded the fire to be cool and safe for him.

The lesson for Muslim youth: You will be surrounded by social, cultural, and peer 'idols' — materialism, status, haram relationships, and cultural traditions that contradict Islam. Ibrahim's courage to declare 'I am free of what you worship' is the model. You don't need to destroy physical objects; destroy the idols in your own heart.
sunday.source: Quran 21:51-70; Quran 2:258-260; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-Anbiya; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: Musa (AS) and Bani Isra'il — Gratitude After Deliverance
sunday.arabic_text: وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ لَئِن شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ وَلَئِن كَفَرْتُمْ إِنَّ عَذَابِي لَشَدِيدٌ
sunday.english_text: And remember when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you in favor; but if you deny, indeed My punishment is severe. (Quran 14:7)
sunday.lesson:
After Allah rescued Bani Isra'il from the tyranny of Pharaoh — parting the sea, sending manna and quails, giving them the Torah — they repeatedly fell into ingratitude, idol worship, and complaint. Despite this, Allah continued to guide them through Musa (AS).

For corps members: You have been given health, education, an opportunity to serve — blessings countless others lack. Ingratitude takes the form of complaining about your posting, neglecting Salah despite having time, and forgetting that every moment of the service year is from Allah's favor. Shukr (gratitude) multiplies blessings; kufr al-ni'mah (ingratitude for blessings) removes them.
sunday.source: Quran 14:7; Quran 2:47-61; Tafsir as-Sa'di, Surah Ibrahim; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

monday.title: Hadith on Modesty (Haya')
monday.english_text: Modesty brings nothing but good.
monday.chain_of_narration: Imran ibn Husayn → Abu Qilabah → Ayyub as-Sakhtiyani → Hammad ibn Zayd
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Imran ibn Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (6117) and Sahih Muslim (37).
monday.lesson: Haya' (modesty/shyness) is a branch of faith. It governs how you dress, how you speak, how you interact with the opposite gender, and how you conduct yourself in public. Far from being a weakness, the Prophet described it as bringing only good. A corps member with haya' stands out as a person of character in any community.
monday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6117; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 37; Sharh Riyad as-Salihin by Shaykh Ibn al-'Uthaymeen

monday.title: Hadith on Avoiding What Does Not Concern You
monday.arabic_text: مِنْ حُسْنِ إِسْلَامِ الْمَرْءِ تَرْكُهُ مَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ
monday.english_text: Part of a person's excellence in Islam is leaving what does not concern him.
monday.transliteration: Min husni islaamil-mar'i tarkuhu maa la ya'neeh.
monday.chain_of_narration: Abu Hurayrah (RA) → through several chains; also from al-Husayn ibn Ali → Imam Malik → considered sahih by Ibn Rajab
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Jami' al-Tirmidhi (2317) and Ibn Majah (3976), classified as Hasan.
monday.lesson: This hadith is considered one of the foundational principles of Islam. Unnecessary involvement in others' affairs, gossip, minding other corps members' drama, wasting time on irrelevant social media debates — all of these are symptoms of poor spiritual health. Guard your time and attention this service year.
monday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 2317; Ibn Majah, Hadith 3976; Jami' al-Ulum wal-Hikam by Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali, Hadith 12

tuesday.title: Morning Dhikr — La ilaha illallah Wahdahu
tuesday.arabic_text: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
tuesday.english_text: There is no god but Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belongs all dominion, and to Him belongs all praise, and He has power over all things.
tuesday.transliteration: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, lahul mulku wa lahul hamdu wa Huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadeer.
tuesday.benefits: Whoever says this 100 times in the morning has the reward equivalent to freeing 10 slaves, 100 good deeds are recorded for him, 100 sins are wiped away, and he is protected from Shaytan until evening. A single 15-second dhikr with this much reward — do not miss your mornings.
tuesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3293; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2691; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

tuesday.title: Du'a Upon Waking — Alhamdulillahilladhi ahyana
tuesday.arabic_text: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
tuesday.english_text: All praise is due to Allah who gave us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.
tuesday.transliteration: Alhamdulillahilladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur.
tuesday.benefits: This is the prescribed du'a upon waking from sleep. Sleep is described in the Quran as a 'minor death' (Quran 39:42). Every morning you wake up is a new gift of life from Allah. Beginning the day with this dhikr sets a tone of gratitude and reminds the Muslim that death is real and the resurrection is certain.
tuesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6312; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

wednesday.title: The Danger of Shirk — The Unforgivable Sin
wednesday.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَاءُ
wednesday.english_text: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. (Quran 4:48)
wednesday.lesson: Shirk (associating partners with Allah) is the only sin Allah has declared He will not forgive if one dies upon it. This makes Tawheed not merely a theological concept but a matter of eternal survival. Understanding what constitutes shirk — and what does not — is obligatory for every Muslim. The scholar Ibn al-Qayyim said: 'The whole of the Quran is about Tawheed.'
wednesday.extra_notes:
Real-life scenario: A corps member who is sick is advised by colleagues to visit a local shrine or herbalist who claims spiritual powers. Going to such places and believing in their powers is major shirk in Tawheed al-Uluhiyyah — directing hope and fear to other than Allah in matters only Allah controls.

Q: What about using black seed (Nigella sativa) or ruqyah (Quranic healing)? Is that shirk?
A: No. Black seed is a Sunnah remedy. Ruqyah using Quran and authentic du'a is permissible and recommended. The distinction is: using permitted means while trusting Allah as the Healer. Shirk begins when you believe the means themselves have independent power apart from Allah.
wednesday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 4:48; Kitab at-Tawheed by Ibn Abd al-Wahhab; Al-Jawab al-Kafi by Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyyah

wednesday.title: Tawakkul — True Reliance on Allah
wednesday.arabic_text: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ
wednesday.english_text: And whoever relies upon Allah — then He is sufficient for him. (Quran 65:3)
wednesday.lesson:
Tawakkul is not passivity — it is not refusing to seek medical treatment or abandoning your duties and saying 'Allah will provide.' True tawakkul is taking all permissible means while placing your heart's reliance on Allah alone. The Prophet said: 'Tie your camel, then put your trust in Allah.' (Tirmidhi, Hasan).

For corps members: Apply for a good posting while trusting Allah with the outcome. Study hard for your exams while knowing that results come from Allah. Tawakkul means your heart is at peace regardless of outcome because you know Allah is in control.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: How do I distinguish between tawakkul and laziness?
A: A person of tawakkul does everything within their capacity, then surrenders the result to Allah. A lazy person fails to do their part and calls it tawakkul. Ibn al-Qayyim distinguished: 'The person of tawakkul is the busiest person — in taking means. But his heart is the calmest — in surrendering to Allah.'
wednesday.source: Tafsir as-Sa'di, Quran 65:3; Madarij as-Salikin by Ibn al-Qayyim; Al-Fawa'id by Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyyah

thursday.title: Fiqh of Salah — Times of Prayer
thursday.arabic_text: إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ كَانَتْ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتَابًا مَّوْقُوتًا
thursday.english_text: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times. (Quran 4:103)
thursday.lesson: The five daily prayers have fixed time windows set by Allah. Fajr: from dawn until sunrise. Dhuhr: from midday until an object's shadow equals its length. Asr: from end of Dhuhr time until sunset (with difference between madhabs on exact calculation). Maghrib: from sunset until twilight disappears. Isha: from end of Maghrib until midnight (preferred) or dawn (permissible with excuse). A corps member must know these times even without a smartphone app.
thursday.extra_notes:
Q: My supervisor refuses to allow me to pray during work hours. What do I do?
A: Diplomatically inform your supervisor that prayer is a constitutional right in Nigeria. If refused, consult MCAN leadership. In the meantime, if prayers can be combined: Dhuhr and Asr may be combined when traveling or in hardship (Hanbali and Shafi'i allow this; Maliki and Hanafi generally do not without severe necessity). Jamul-ta'kheer (combining by delay) of Dhuhr with Asr and Maghrib with Isha is the more commonly allowed combination.

Note: Missing Salah deliberately without excuse is a major sin. Missing it by forgetting: pray as soon as you remember (Hadith: Bukhari 597).
thursday.source: Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq, Vol. 1; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah; Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli

thursday.title: Fiqh of Qiblah — Facing the Direction of Prayer
thursday.arabic_text: فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَحَيْثُمَا كُنتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ
thursday.english_text: Turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it. (Quran 2:144)
thursday.lesson: Facing the Qiblah (direction of the Ka'bah in Makkah) is a condition for the validity of prayer for one who is able. For those in Nigeria, the Qiblah is generally toward the northeast. If you are unsure of the direction in a new posting location, use a compass app, ask locals, or align with the nearest mosque's prayer direction. If the direction is unknown and cannot be determined, make your best effort — Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
thursday.extra_notes:
Q: My prayer mat in a hotel room may not face the exact Qiblah. Is my prayer valid?
A: Yes. Scholars say what is required is to face the general direction (jiha) of the Qiblah, not the exact point (ayn), for those at a distance from Makkah. Use a compass, do your best, and your prayer is valid.

Exception: The Prophet permitted voluntary prayers (nafl) while traveling on a riding animal or vehicle, facing whatever direction the animal was heading. (Sahih Muslim 700)
thursday.source: Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli; Bidayat al-Mujtahid by Ibn Rushd; Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq

friday.title: The Khutbah — Listening as an Act of Worship
friday.arabic_text: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ الْقُرْآنُ فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وَأَنصِتُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ
friday.english_text: And when the Quran is recited, listen to it attentively and be silent so that you may receive mercy. (Quran 7:204)
friday.lesson:
Scholars extend this verse's ruling to the Jumu'ah khutbah. The Hanbali and Shafi'i scholars hold that speaking during the khutbah nullifies the reward of Jumu'ah. Even saying 'be quiet' to a noisy person is impermissible once the khutbah begins. The Maliki school permits a brief utterance for necessity.

Practical guidance: Arrive early, silence your phone, find a spot without distractions, and listen with the intention of implementing what you hear. A khutbah heard with attentiveness is a weekly renewal of your spiritual contract with Allah.
friday.extra_notes:
Q: What if the khutbah is entirely in Arabic and I don't understand it?
A: Scholars differ. Many hold the khutbah must be in Arabic as part of the rite. However, Hanafi scholars permit vernacular explanations alongside Arabic. If your local masjid delivers a full Hausa or Yoruba khutbah, follow the ruling of a qualified scholar in your area.
friday.source: Quran 7:204; Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq; Sharh al-Mumti' by Shaykh Ibn al-'Uthaymeen; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah

friday.title: Friday Azkar — Du'a of the Distressed
friday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْهَمِّ وَالْحَزَنِ، وَالْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ، وَالْبُخْلِ وَالْجُبْنِ، وَضَلَعِ الدَّيْنِ وَغَلَبَةِ الرِّجَالِ
friday.english_text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from miserliness and cowardice, from the burden of debt and the overpowering of men.
friday.transliteration: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-hammi wal-hazan, wal-'ajzi wal-kasal, wal-bukhli wal-jubn, wa dala'id-dayni wa ghalabatir-rijal.
friday.benefits: This du'a from Sahih al-Bukhari covers eight of the most common afflictions of a young Muslim — anxiety about the future, grief from the past, incapacity, laziness, stinginess, cowardice, debt, and social pressure. Every corps member will face several of these. Making this du'a every Friday is spiritual insurance against these enemies of productivity.
friday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 2893; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Du'a; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

saturday.title: Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) — From Enemy to Champion of Islam
saturday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ أَعِزَّ الْإِسْلَامَ بِأَحَبِّ هَذَيْنِ الرَّجُلَيْنِ إِلَيْكَ: بِأَبِي جَهْلٍ أَوْ بِعُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ
saturday.english_text: O Allah, strengthen Islam with the more beloved of these two men to You: Abu Jahl or Umar ibn al-Khattab.
saturday.lesson:
Before his conversion, Umar ibn al-Khattab was one of the fiercest enemies of Islam, to the point that he set out to kill the Prophet himself. Allah answered the Prophet's du'a and guided Umar — and Islam gained one of its greatest champions. Umar's conversion was so powerful that the Muslims could finally pray openly in Makkah for the first time.

As the second Caliph, Umar was known for his justice, his firmness in truth, his humility before Allah, and his tearing down of social hierarchies. He slept on the ground while leading the greatest empire of his time.

Lesson: Never despair of anyone's guidance. And never assume that your own faith is secure without constant renewal. Umar, despite his greatness, regularly asked companions: 'Have you heard me mentioned as a hypocrite by the Prophet?' Such was his fear of Allah.
saturday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 3683; Al-Bidayah wan-Nihayah by Ibn Kathir; As-Seerah an-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham

saturday.title: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) — The Ambassador of Islam
saturday.arabic_text: مَا رَأَيْتُ بِمَكَّةَ أَحَدًا أَنْعَمَ مِنْ مُصْعَبِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ
saturday.english_text: I did not see anyone in Makkah who was more pampered than Mus'ab ibn Umayr.
saturday.lesson:
Mus'ab ibn Umayr was among the wealthiest and most fashionable young men of Makkah. When he embraced Islam, his family disowned him and cut off his wealth. He went from wearing the finest clothes to wearing a single patched garment — yet he never regretted his choice. The Prophet sent him to Madinah as the first Islamic ambassador, and through his gentle da'wah, whole tribes embraced Islam.

Lesson for corps members: Youth, education, and social skills are gifts. Like Mus'ab, use your gifts in the service of Islam. He was the Prophet's choice for da'wah because of his refinement, articulateness, and character — not his wealth. Your skills in your PPA community can open doors no one else can open.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3924; Usud al-Ghabah by Ibn al-Athir; As-Seerah an-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1

sunday.title: Nuh (AS) — 950 Years of Patience in Da'wah
sunday.arabic_text: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِي لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا فَلَمْ يَزِدْهُمْ دُعَائِي إِلَّا فِرَارًا
sunday.english_text: He said: My Lord, I have called my people night and day, but my calling only increased them in flight. (Quran 71:5-6)
sunday.lesson:
Nuh (AS) preached to his people for 950 years. They mocked him, covered their ears, and only a small number believed. Yet Nuh did not give up. He called them privately, publicly, gently, and boldly. When the punishment came, Allah saved the believers on the Ark.

For corps members: When your da'wah or good influence in your community seems to have no effect — remember Nuh. Success in da'wah is not measured by how many people accept; it is measured by your sincerity and effort. Plant the seed; leave the harvest to Allah.
sunday.source: Quran 71:1-28; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Nuh; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir; Quran 11:25-49

sunday.title: Luqman (AS) — Wisdom to His Son
sunday.arabic_text: يَا بُنَيَّ أَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ وَأْمُرْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَانْهَ عَنِ الْمُنكَرِ وَاصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا أَصَابَكَ
sunday.english_text: O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. (Quran 31:17)
sunday.lesson:
Luqman was a wise man — not a prophet — whose counsel to his son Allah immortalized in the Quran. His advice covers the pillars of a righteous life: Tawheed (do not associate partners with Allah), good character, establishing prayer, commanding good and forbidding evil, and patience.

The wisdom of Luqman is the complete roadmap for a Muslim corps member's year of service. Establish your prayer first. Then be an agent of good in your community. Forbid wrong where you have authority. And when hardship comes — and it will — be patient.
sunday.source: Quran 31:12-19; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Luqman; Tafsir as-Sa'di, Surah Luqman

monday.title: Hadith on the Rights of the Muslim
monday.arabic_text: حَقُّ الْمُسْلِمِ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِ سِتٌّ: إِذَا لَقِيتَهُ فَسَلِّمْ عَلَيْهِ، وَإِذَا دَعَاكَ فَأَجِبْهُ
monday.english_text: The rights of a Muslim upon a Muslim are six: when you meet him, greet him with salaam; when he invites you, respond; when he seeks your advice, advise him sincerely; when he sneezes and praises Allah, say 'yarhamukallah'; when he is sick, visit him; and when he dies, follow his funeral.
monday.chain_of_narration: Abu Hurayrah (RA) → Sa'id al-Maqburi → Malik ibn Anas
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih Muslim (2162).
monday.lesson: Muslim brotherhood is not sentimental — it has practical obligations. A corps member who greets fellow Muslims, attends to the sick among them, and gives sincere advice is fulfilling a religious duty. These six rights are the glue of the Muslim community.
monday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2162; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Rights of Muslims; Sharh Sahih Muslim by Imam an-Nawawi

monday.title: Hadith on Removing Harm from the Path
monday.arabic_text: الإِيمَانُ بِضْعٌ وَسَبْعُونَ شُعْبَةً، فَأَفْضَلُهَا قَوْلُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَأَدْنَاهَا إِمَاطَةُ الأَذَى عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ
monday.english_text: Faith has over seventy branches. The highest is saying 'La ilaha illallah,' and the lowest is removing harm from a path.
monday.transliteration: Al-imanu bid'un wa sab'una shu'bah, fa-afdaluha qawlu la ilaha illallah, wa adnaha imaatatul-adha 'anit-tariq.
monday.chain_of_narration: Abu Hurayrah (RA) → Abu Salih → Suhayb → Ibn Abi Dhi'b
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (9) and Sahih Muslim (35).
monday.lesson: Even the most 'minor' act — moving a stone, a thorn, or a branch from a path — is a branch of faith. For corps members doing community service, this hadith transforms even the most humble physical task into an act of worship. No clean-up exercise, no well-digging, no road clearing is beneath your faith.
monday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 9; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 35; Jami' al-Ulum wal-Hikam by Ibn Rajab

tuesday.title: Du'a Before Eating
tuesday.arabic_text: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ
tuesday.english_text: In the name of Allah.
tuesday.transliteration: Bismillah.
tuesday.benefits: The Prophet instructed: 'When one of you eats, let him mention the name of Allah. If he forgets to mention the name of Allah at the beginning, let him say: Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirah (In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end).' Saying Bismillah before eating prevents Shaytan from partaking in the food and its blessings. A small act, but its consistent performance marks the believer throughout the day.
tuesday.source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 3767; Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 1858; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

tuesday.title: Du'a When Leaving Home
tuesday.arabic_text: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
tuesday.english_text: In the name of Allah. I put my trust in Allah. There is no power or strength except with Allah.
tuesday.transliteration: Bismillahi, tawakkaltu 'alallahi, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.
tuesday.benefits: The Prophet said: 'Whoever says this when leaving his home will be told: You are guided, defended, and protected. The shaytan will stay away from him.' For a corps member leaving for work, CDS, or any activity — this du'a is a shield for the day. It is light on the tongue yet comprehensive in protection.
tuesday.source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 5095; Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 3426 (Hasan Sahih); Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

wednesday.title: Al-Wala wal-Bara — Loyalty and Disavowal for Allah's Sake
wednesday.arabic_text: لَّا يَتَّخِذِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِن دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
wednesday.english_text: Believers should not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers. (Quran 3:28)
wednesday.lesson: Al-Wala wal-Bara (loyalty and disavowal) is a fundamental aspect of Tawheed. It means loving and supporting what Allah loves, and distancing oneself from what Allah has forbidden. This does NOT mean being rude or hostile to non-Muslims — the Prophet interacted kindly and justly with non-Muslims. It means your deepest loyalties and closest confidants are among those who share your faith and values.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Common misconception: Does al-Wala wal-Bara mean I can't have non-Muslim friends or colleagues?
Answer: No. The prohibition is against taking non-Muslims as awliya' — those to whom you turn for your deepest guidance, whom you obey over Allah's commandments, or who undermine your faith. Interacting respectfully, cooperating on shared goals, and treating non-Muslims with justice and kindness is fully permitted and encouraged. The Prophet ate with, traded with, and spoke fairly to people of other faiths.

Real-life scenario: If your non-Muslim colleagues pressure you to skip Jumu'ah, drink alcohol, or compromise your Islamic standards — that is where the boundaries of wala' become relevant.
wednesday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 3:28; Al-Wala wal-Bara by Shaykh Muhammad Sa'id al-Qahtani; Al-Aqeedah al-Wasitiyyah by Ibn Taymiyyah

wednesday.title: Loving the Prophet — A Pillar of Iman
wednesday.arabic_text: لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى أَكُونَ أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ وَالِدِهِ وَوَلَدِهِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ
wednesday.english_text: None of you truly believes until I am more beloved to him than his father, his child, and all of mankind.
wednesday.lesson:
Loving the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not optional — it is a condition of complete faith. This love is expressed through: following his Sunnah, defending his honor when it is attacked, feeling pain when his teachings are mocked, and longing to meet him in Jannah.

This love is distinct from worship (ibadah), which belongs to Allah alone. We love the Prophet as we love the greatest of human beings, the one through whom we received our religion. Imam al-Nawawi said: 'Loving the Prophet more than oneself means one should not prefer one's desires over the Prophet's commands.'
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: Is celebrating the Mawlid (Prophet's birthday) an expression of this love?
A: Scholars differ. Those who permit it say it is a way of expressing love for the Prophet, provided there are no prohibited elements. Those who disallow it argue it is an innovation (bid'ah) with no precedent in the first three generations. The majority ruling of classical Sunni scholars permits it with conditions, while the Salafi-influenced scholars prohibit it. Both groups agree that the Prophet must be loved — they differ only on this specific expression.
wednesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 15; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 44; Sharh Sahih Muslim by Imam an-Nawawi

thursday.title: Fiqh of Fasting — Conditions and Pillars of Sawm
thursday.arabic_text: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ
thursday.english_text: O you who have believed, fasting has been decreed upon you as it was decreed upon those before you. (Quran 2:183)
thursday.lesson: The pillars of Sawm (fasting) are: intention made before Fajr, and abstaining from food, drink, and sexual relations from Fajr to Maghrib. Among the conditions for obligation: being Muslim, adult (baligh), sane, capable, and resident (not traveling). Those excused include: the traveler, the sick, the elderly (who cannot fast), and women during menstruation or postnatal bleeding. Those who miss fasts must make them up (qada') at the earliest opportunity.
thursday.extra_notes:
Q: Is voluntary fasting (e.g., Mondays and Thursdays) affected if I am traveling?
A: Scholars recommend breaking voluntary fasts while traveling to avoid hardship. If it causes no hardship, you may continue. The Prophet fasted and broke his fast during different journeys depending on circumstance.

Practical note: The 'white days' — the 13th, 14th, and 15th of every lunar month — are Sunnah fasting days. Corps members can begin this practice as a regular act of worship throughout their service year.
thursday.source: Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli, Vol. 3; Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq; Sharh al-Mumti' by Ibn al-'Uthaymeen

thursday.title: Fiqh of Halal and Haram Food
thursday.arabic_text: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُلُوا مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ
thursday.english_text: O you who have believed, eat from the good things which We have provided for you. (Quran 2:172)
thursday.lesson:
Halal food is a religious obligation, not merely a preference. Prohibited are: pork and its by-products, blood, carrion (dead animals not slaughtered), animals not slaughtered in Allah's name, intoxicants, and animals with fangs (predatory animals). All seafood is halal according to the majority. Zabiha (proper Islamic slaughter) is required for land animals.

For a corps member posted to a non-Muslim-majority area: Seek markets or butchers who provide halal meat. In the absence of halal meat, fish and permissible plant food are always available alternatives. It is not permissible to eat pork or haram meat out of social pressure or convenience.
thursday.extra_notes:
Q: Can I eat food cooked in the same pot as pork if I just arrived at a new posting?
A: No. Pork contamination renders food impermissible. You may politely decline such food without causing offence. Carry your own provisions when possible.

Q: What about gelatin in processed foods — is it halal?
A: If the gelatin source is unknown, most contemporary scholars advise avoiding it as a precaution. If it is certified halal or derived from fish/plants, it is permissible.
thursday.source: Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli; Halal and Haram in Islam by Yusuf al-Qaradawi; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah

friday.title: Ghusl on Friday — Obligation or Sunnah?
friday.arabic_text: غُسْلُ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ وَاجِبٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُحْتَلِمٍ
friday.english_text: Ghusl (bathing) on Friday is obligatory upon every adult.
friday.lesson: The apparent text of this hadith suggests obligation (wujub). However, the majority of scholars — Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali in one narration — hold it to be a strongly recommended Sunnah (Sunnah Mu'akkadah), not strictly obligatory, based on other hadith that soften the ruling. The Hanbali madhab has a view that it is wajib for men attending Jumu'ah. Regardless of the juridical category: bathing on Friday before Jumu'ah is among the most emphasized Sunnah acts of the week. Do not miss it.
friday.extra_notes:
Complete pre-Jumu'ah preparation checklist:
1. Perform ghusl (full bath) on Friday morning
2. Cut nails if needed
3. Apply perfume (men only)
4. Wear best/cleanest clothes
5. Use miswak (tooth-stick)
6. Go to the masjid early
7. Pray nafl upon entering
8. Read Surah al-Kahf before the prayer
9. Listen to the khutbah with full attention
10. Make abundant du'a in the last hour before Maghrib
friday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 879; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 846; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah; Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq

friday.title: Friday Azkar — Seeking Refuge from the Dajjal
friday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ، وَمِنْ عَذَابِ النَّارِ، وَمِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْمَحْيَا وَالْمَمَاتِ، وَمِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْمَسِيحِ الدَّجَّالِ
friday.english_text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, from the punishment of the Fire, from the trials of life and death, and from the trial of the False Messiah (Dajjal).
friday.transliteration: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min 'adhabil-qabr, wa min 'adhabin-naar, wa min fitnatil-mahya wal-mamaat, wa min fitnatil-masihid-dajjal.
friday.benefits: This du'a is to be said after the final tashahhud in every prayer. But on Friday — when the first and last ten verses of Surah al-Kahf are recited and this du'a is made — the Muslim builds a comprehensive shield against the greatest tribulation before the Day of Judgment. The Dajjal represents the trial of deception, materialism, and moral confusion — the very tests facing Muslim youth today.
friday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 1377; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 588; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

saturday.title: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) — The Lion of Allah
saturday.arabic_text: أَنَا مَدِينَةُ الْعِلْمِ وَعَلِيٌّ بَابُهَا
saturday.english_text: I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate.
saturday.lesson:
Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) was the first child to embrace Islam, the cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet, and one of the ten companions promised Paradise. He was known for his extraordinary courage in battle — earning the title 'Asadullah' (Lion of Allah) — and for his profound knowledge of the Quran and Islamic jurisprudence. He was the fourth Caliph of Islam.

Ali's early conversion as a child is a powerful reminder: faith is not the privilege of age. Many of the greatest companions entered Islam as young people. Your youth is your asset, not your limitation. Use these NYSC years to build knowledge of your deen as Ali did — for knowledge protects you in every arena of life.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3701; Usud al-Ghabah by Ibn al-Athir; Tarikh al-Khulafa by Imam as-Suyuti

saturday.title: Fatimah bint Muhammad (RA) — The Leader of Women in Paradise
saturday.arabic_text: فَاطِمَةُ سَيِّدَةُ نِسَاءِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ
saturday.english_text: Fatimah is the leader of the women of the people of Paradise.
saturday.lesson:
Fatimah (RA) was the youngest daughter of the Prophet and his most beloved child. She lived a life of poverty by choice, grinding grain by hand while her father was the leader of the Muslim community, because she understood that the Hereafter was the real goal. She bore hardship, loss, and trials with remarkable dignity.

The Prophet wept over her when she visited him on his deathbed and whispered to her that she would be the first of his family to join him. She passed away six months after him.

Lesson for corps members: Proximity to the blessings of this world is not the measure of success. Fatimah's closeness was to the Prophet and to Allah. Seek that closeness above all worldly achievement.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3623; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2450; Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani

sunday.title: Musa (AS) and Pharaoh — Courage Before Tyrants
sunday.arabic_text: اذْهَبَا إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَىٰ فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَّيِّنًا لَّعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ
sunday.english_text: Go both of you to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed. And speak to him with gentle words — perhaps he may be reminded or fear Allah. (Quran 20:43-44)
sunday.lesson:
Musa and Harun (AS) were sent to Pharaoh — the most powerful tyrant of their time, who claimed divinity. Yet Allah instructed them to speak 'gently.' This is the Islamic methodology of speaking truth to power: firmly in content, gently in style.

Musa had a speech impediment, a fugitive past in Egypt, and no worldly power — yet Allah sent him to the greatest king of the earth. For corps members working in challenging political and social environments: speak truth, maintain Islamic ethics, but do so with wisdom and gentleness. Allah equips those He sends.
sunday.source: Quran 20:9-79; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Ta-Ha; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: The Companions of the Trench — Ahl al-Ukhdood
sunday.arabic_text: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُوا فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ
sunday.english_text: Indeed, those who tortured the believing men and believing women and then did not repent will have the punishment of Hellfire. (Quran 85:10)
sunday.lesson:
Surah al-Buruj describes a tyrannical king who dug trenches and threw believers into fires for refusing to abandon their faith. The believers died rather than deny Allah. The Quran memorializes their sacrifice — their names are unknown, but their reward with Allah is eternal.

Lesson: There are moments when faith costs something real. The corps member who refuses to compromise their salah, their dress code, or their ethics under workplace pressure is, in a small but real way, standing with the believers of the trench. The cost of holding firm is always less than the cost of compromise.
sunday.source: Quran 85:1-22; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-Buruj; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 3005 (story of the Boy and the King)

monday.title: Hadith on Controlling Anger
monday.arabic_text: لَيْسَ الشَّدِيدُ بِالصُّرَعَةِ، إِنَّمَا الشَّدِيدُ الَّذِي يَمْلِكُ نَفْسَهُ عِنْدَ الْغَضَبِ
monday.english_text: The strong man is not the one who wrestles others down. The strong man is the one who controls himself when angry.
monday.chain_of_narration: Abu Hurayrah (RA) → Hamid ibn Abd ar-Rahman → several chains to Imam Malik
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (6114) and Sahih Muslim (2609).
monday.lesson: Anger is the entry point of Shaytan. The Prophet defined real strength not as physical power but as mastery of the nafs (self). For a corps member navigating difficult supervisors, unfair postings, or frustrating teammates — controlling your anger is a daily act of Islamic strength. The Prophet's advice: sit if standing, lie down if sitting, perform wudu, and seek refuge from Shaytan.
monday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6114; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2609; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Anger

monday.title: Hadith on Seeking Knowledge
monday.arabic_text: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
monday.english_text: Whoever treads a path in search of knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise.
monday.transliteration: Man salaka tareeqan yaltamisu feehi 'ilman sahhalallahu lahu bihi tareeqan ilal-jannah.
monday.chain_of_narration: Abu Hurayrah (RA) → transmitted through multiple sahih chains
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih Muslim (2699).
monday.lesson: Allah has linked the pursuit of knowledge directly to Jannah. Whether you are studying for professional certification, learning the Quran, or attending Islamic lectures — every step toward genuine knowledge is a step toward Paradise. Use your posting period to learn something new every day.
monday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2699; Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 2646; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Knowledge

tuesday.title: Du'a When Entering the Masjid
tuesday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ
tuesday.english_text: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.
tuesday.transliteration: Allahummaf-tah lee abwaba rahmatik.
tuesday.benefits: Upon entering the masjid, one should enter with the right foot first, recite this du'a, and pray two rak'ahs of tahiyyat al-masjid (greeting of the mosque) before sitting. The masjid is Allah's house — entering it with proper etiquette and du'a transforms every visit into a complete act of worship from the moment you step inside.
tuesday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 713; Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith 772; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

tuesday.title: Du'a When Leaving the Masjid
tuesday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ
tuesday.english_text: O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty.
tuesday.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik.
tuesday.benefits: Upon leaving the masjid, exit with the left foot first and recite this du'a. The believer leaves the House of Allah and steps into the world — seeking Allah's provision as they return to their daily affairs. This du'a bridges the spiritual and the material, reminding us that rizq (provision) also comes from Allah.
tuesday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 713; Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith 773; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

wednesday.title: Bid'ah — Innovation in Religion
wednesday.arabic_text: وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَمُحْدَثَاتِ الْأُمُورِ فَإِنَّ كُلَّ مُحْدَثَةٍ بِدْعَةٌ وَكُلَّ بِدْعَةٍ ضَلَالَةٌ
wednesday.english_text: Beware of newly invented matters, for every newly invented matter is an innovation, and every innovation is misguidance.
wednesday.lesson: Bid'ah (religious innovation) refers to introducing into acts of worship things that have no basis in the Quran or authentic Sunnah, with the intention of drawing closer to Allah. The Sunnah is complete; the Prophet left nothing of the religion out. Scholars distinguish between bid'ah hasanah (accepted by some as praiseworthy innovations in worldly matters) and bid'ah in acts of worship, which all agree is forbidden.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Real-life scenario: Some people add specific prayers or rituals for 'special nights' not established in the Sunnah, believing they have extra reward. The Muslim must ask: Did the Prophet or his companions do this? If not, it requires strong evidence before practice.

Q: Is using microphones for the adhan bid'ah?
A: No. Scholars distinguish between bid'ah in the form/essence of worship (adding a new rak'ah) and using new means for an existing worship. Microphones are tools, not acts of worship in themselves. The Sunnah form of adhan is preserved; only the amplification method has changed.
wednesday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 867; Al-I'tisam by Imam al-Shatibi; Iqtida' as-Sirat al-Mustaqim by Ibn Taymiyyah

wednesday.title: Istighfar — Seeking Forgiveness as Tawheed
wednesday.arabic_text: سَيِّدُ الاسْتِغْفَارِ أَنْ تَقُولَ: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ
wednesday.english_text: The master supplication of forgiveness is to say: O Allah, You are my Lord. There is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant.
wednesday.lesson: Seeking forgiveness (istighfar) is an act of Tawheed because it acknowledges that: only Allah can forgive sins, we are dependent servants, and no intermediary is needed between us and Allah. The Prophet — who had no sins — sought forgiveness more than 70 times a day. What about us? Constant istighfar is both a form of worship and a practical cleansing of the spiritual heart.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: Do I need a sheikh or imam to make istighfar on my behalf?
A: In Sunni theology, no. Every Muslim can make tawbah (repentance) directly to Allah without any intermediary. The conditions of valid tawbah are: stopping the sin, genuine remorse, firm intention not to return to it, and if rights of others were violated, making restitution.
wednesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6306; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Istighfar; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

thursday.title: Fiqh of Marriage — Conditions and Pillars
thursday.arabic_text: يَا مَعْشَرَ الشَّبَابِ مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ مِنْكُمُ الْبَاءَةَ فَلْيَتَزَوَّجْ
thursday.english_text: O young people! Whoever among you can afford marriage, let him marry.
thursday.lesson:
The pillars of Islamic marriage (nikah) are: offer and acceptance (ijab and qabul), the wali (guardian, usually the father) for the bride, two Muslim witnesses, and the mahr (dowry gift to the bride). Marriage is Sunnah Mu'akkadah and becomes obligatory when one fears falling into haram. The Prophet said it 'lowers the gaze and protects the private parts.'

For corps members: If you are already married, honor your spouse's rights even from a distance. If unmarried, use this year to prepare — financially, spiritually, and in maturity. Rushing into inappropriate relationships during service year is among the most common mistakes of young Muslims.
thursday.extra_notes:
Q: Can a couple get married without telling their parents during service year?
A: A nikah without the wali (guardian) of the woman is invalid according to the majority of scholars (Shafi'i, Maliki, Hanbali). The Hanafi school allows a mature woman to contract her own marriage with witnesses. Regardless of madhab, marrying secretly or without parental knowledge causes harm to family relationships and often leads to greater problems later.
thursday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 5066; Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq, Vol. 2; Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli

thursday.title: Fiqh of Lowering the Gaze
thursday.arabic_text: قُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ وَيَحْفَظُوا فُرُوجَهُمْ
thursday.english_text: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their private parts. (Quran 24:30)
thursday.lesson: Lowering the gaze is a direct Quranic command — not merely recommended but obligatory. The eye is the first step of Zina (unlawful relations), as the Prophet said: 'The zina of the eyes is the gaze.' (Sahih al-Bukhari 6243). In the mixed environments of NYSC orientation camps, offices, and CDS events, intentional lowering of the gaze is a practical act of worship.
thursday.extra_notes:
Q: Is it haram to look at a non-mahram's face accidentally?
A: The first glance that is unintentional is forgiven. The Prophet said: 'The first glance is for you; the second is against you.' (Abu Dawud, Hasan). It is the deliberate second look and beyond that is prohibited.

Q: Can I work professionally alongside non-mahram colleagues?
A: Yes. Working in mixed environments is permissible. What is required: avoid seclusion (khalwah) with a non-mahram, maintain professional boundaries, lower the gaze, and avoid unnecessary personal conversation.
thursday.source: Quran 24:30-31; Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6243; Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli

friday.title: The Best Day the Sun Has Ever Risen Upon
friday.arabic_text: خَيْرُ يَوْمٍ طَلَعَتْ عَلَيْهِ الشَّمْسُ يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَةِ، فِيهِ خُلِقَ آدَمُ، وَفِيهِ أُدْخِلَ الْجَنَّةَ، وَفِيهِ أُخْرِجَ مِنْهَا
friday.english_text: The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was admitted to Paradise, and on it he was expelled from it.
friday.lesson: Friday is cosmically significant in Islamic theology — the day of Adam's creation, entry into Paradise, expulsion, and the Day of Judgment will occur on a Friday. It is a day of intensified worship, community, du'a, and renewal. The Muslim corps member should treat Friday not as a day off but as the spiritual high point of the week.
friday.extra_notes:
Five special deeds on Friday:
1. Read Surah al-Kahf (between Thursday Maghrib and Friday Asr)
2. Send salawat abundantly upon the Prophet
3. Make du'a in the final hour before Maghrib
4. Perform ghusl and go early to Jumu'ah
5. Make tawbah (repentance) — the gates of Jannah are especially open
friday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 854; Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 1046; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Friday

friday.title: Friday Azkar — The Comprehensive Du'a of Ibrahim (AS)
friday.arabic_text: رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةِ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِي رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَاءِ
friday.english_text: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication. (Quran 14:40)
friday.transliteration: Rabbi-j'alni muqeemas-salati wa min dhurriyyati, Rabbana wa taqabbal du'a'.
friday.benefits: This du'a of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) asks for consistency in prayer for oneself and one's future family — and for the acceptance of all du'a. It is among the most beautiful of Quranic supplications because it links personal worship to legacy. A corps member who makes this du'a is planting seeds for righteous children, a righteous home, and a righteous community.
friday.source: Quran 14:40-41; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Ibrahim; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

saturday.title: Uthman ibn Affan (RA) — Generosity That Funded Islam
saturday.arabic_text: مَا ضَرَّ عُثْمَانَ مَا عَمِلَ بَعْدَ الْيَوْمِ
saturday.english_text: Nothing will harm Uthman for what he does after this day.
saturday.lesson:
Uthman ibn Affan (RA) was among the wealthiest companions of the Prophet, yet he used his entire fortune in the service of Islam without hesitation. He equipped the Army of Hardship (Jaysh al-Usrah) single-handedly with 300 fully equipped camels plus horses, weapons, and 1,000 gold dinars. He also purchased the well of Rumah and gave it as a waqf (endowment) for all Muslims, and expanded the Masjid an-Nabawi from his own wealth.

Lesson: Generosity is not proportional to wealth — it is proportional to faith. A corps member earning a modest allowance who gives regularly to sadaqah is following Uthman's example. Your financial contribution to Islamic causes today plants rewards that will grow until the Day of Judgment.
saturday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 3701; Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 2778; As-Seerah an-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham

saturday.title: Aisha bint Abi Bakr (RA) — Mother of the Believers and Scholar of Islam
saturday.arabic_text: خُذُوا شَطْرَ دِينِكُمْ عَنْ هَذِهِ الْحُمَيْرَاءِ
saturday.english_text: Take half of your religion from this red-cheeked woman.
saturday.lesson:
Aisha (RA) was the Prophet's most beloved wife after Khadijah and one of the greatest scholars of Islam. She narrated over 2,000 hadith, corrected companions who made errors in religious matters, taught men and women from behind a screen, and was consulted by senior companions on Islamic rulings after the Prophet's death.

She became a widow at approximately 18 years old and spent the rest of her long life in scholarship and worship. Her knowledge of hadith, fiqh, Arabic poetry, and medicine was extraordinary for her time.

Lesson: Education is for both men and women in Islam. A female corps member who is building her Islamic knowledge is following the path of the Mother of the Believers herself.
saturday.source: Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi; Sahih al-Bukhari, many hadith narrated by Aisha (RA)

sunday.title: Dawud (AS) — Justice, Wisdom, and Repentance
sunday.arabic_text: وَشَدَدْنَا مُلْكَهُ وَآتَيْنَاهُ الْحِكْمَةَ وَفَصْلَ الْخِطَابِ
sunday.english_text: And We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and discernment in speech. (Quran 38:20)
sunday.lesson:
Dawud (AS) was a shepherd who became a king, a warrior who became a prophet, and a man who made a grave mistake — yet returned to Allah with sincere repentance and was forgiven. Allah gave him the Zabur (Psalms), the ability to speak the language of birds, the softening of iron in his hands, and the skill of making armor.

His story teaches the corps member: No matter how high you rise, humility before Allah is the foundation of every achievement. And no matter how deeply you fall through sin, sincere tawbah always opens the door back to Allah.
sunday.source: Quran 38:17-26; Quran 21:78-80; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Sad; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: Sulayman (AS) — Power Used in Service of Allah
sunday.arabic_text: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكًا لَّا يَنبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِي
sunday.english_text: My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. (Quran 38:35)
sunday.lesson:
Sulayman (AS) was given dominion over humans, jinn, animals, birds, and wind — the most expansive kingdom in human history. Yet when an ant colony was about to be crushed by his army, he heard the ant's warning to its people, smiled, and ordered his army to stop. The most powerful man alive stopped for an ant.

Lesson for corps members: Power, authority, and position are tests. The sign of true Islamic leadership is not the crushing of the small but the protection of the weak. Whether you are leading a CDS project or managing a community programme — remember Sulayman and the ant.
sunday.source: Quran 27:15-44; Quran 38:30-40; Tafsir as-Sa'di, Surah an-Naml; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

monday.title: Hadith on the Tongue
monday.arabic_text: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
monday.english_text: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent.
monday.transliteration: Man kaana yu'minu billahi wal-yawmil-akhiri falyaqul khayran aw liyasmut.
monday.chain_of_narration: Abu Hurayrah (RA) → Sa'id al-Musayyib → multiple chains
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (6018) and Sahih Muslim (47).
monday.lesson: The tongue is the most dangerous organ in the human body. More people have destroyed friendships, communities, and their own Hereafter through speech than through any physical act. The standard is simple: before speaking, ask — is this good? If not certain, be silent. Corps members should apply this to group chats, CDS meetings, community interactions, and social media.
monday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6018; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 47; Jami' al-Ulum wal-Hikam by Ibn Rajab, Hadith 15

monday.title: Hadith on Backbiting (Ghibah)
monday.arabic_text: أَتَدْرُونَ مَا الْغِيبَةُ؟ قَالُوا: اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ. قَالَ: ذِكْرُكَ أَخَاكَ بِمَا يَكْرَهُ
monday.english_text: Do you know what backbiting is? They said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: Mentioning your brother in a way he would dislike.
monday.transliteration: Atadroona mal-gheebah? Qaalu: Allahu wa rasuluhu a'lam. Qaala: Dhikruka akhaka bima yakrahu.
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih Muslim (2589).
monday.lesson: Backbiting — speaking about someone's true faults behind their back — is compared in the Quran to eating the flesh of your dead brother (49:12). The definition is important: it doesn't matter whether it is true. If you mention a true fault of someone in their absence and they would dislike it, that is ghibah and it is haram. The exception is speaking to authorities for redress of wrong.
monday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2589; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 49:12; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Backbiting

tuesday.title: Istighfar — Sayyid al-Istighfar
