tuesday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
tuesday.english_text: O Allah, You are my Lord. There is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant. I am upon Your covenant and promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your blessing upon me and I acknowledge my sin. So forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.
tuesday.transliteration: Allahumma anta Rabbee la ilaha illa ant, khalaqtani wa ana 'abduk, wa ana 'ala 'ahdika wa wa'dika mastata't, a'udhu bika min sharri ma sana't, abuu'u laka bini'matika 'alayya, wa abuu'u bidhanbi faghfir lee fa-innahu la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa ant.
tuesday.benefits: The Prophet said: 'Whoever says this with certainty in the morning and dies before evening enters Paradise. And whoever says it with certainty in the evening and dies before morning enters Paradise.' This is the Master of Istighfar — the most comprehensive single supplication for forgiveness. Learn it by heart.
tuesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6306; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

tuesday.title: Dhikr for Anxiety and Worry — La ilaha illa anta subhanaka
tuesday.arabic_text: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
tuesday.english_text: There is no god but You. Glory be to You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers. (Quran 21:87)
tuesday.transliteration: La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu minadh-dhalimeen.
tuesday.benefits: This is the supplication of Yunus (AS) from inside the whale's belly — the darkest place imaginable. The Prophet said: 'No Muslim makes this supplication for anything except that Allah responds to him.' It combines Tawheed, glorification, and confession of fault — the three elements of perfect tawbah. When anxiety, worry, or stress overwhelms a corps member far from home, this is the du'a to turn to.
tuesday.source: Quran 21:87; Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 3505 (Sahih); Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-Anbiya

wednesday.title: The Names of Allah — Al-Hayy and Al-Qayyum
wednesday.arabic_text: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ
wednesday.english_text: Allah — there is no god but He — the Living, the Eternal Sustainer. (Quran 2:255)
wednesday.lesson:
Al-Hayy (The Living) means Allah's life is eternal, perfect, and without beginning or end — unlike created life which is temporary and dependent. Al-Qayyum (The Sustainer) means Allah subsists by Himself and everything in existence subsists only through Him. These are the two greatest of Allah's names — the Prophet said they constitute the greatest name (Ism al-A'dham) through which du'a is always answered.

For the corps member: When you are tired, depleted, or feeling unsupported — remember that Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum never sleeps, never tires, and never stops sustaining you. He is managing your affairs even when you are not aware.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: Which is the greatest name of Allah (Ism al-A'dham)?
A: Scholars have given several answers. Many hold it is 'Allah' itself. Others say 'Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum' based on the hadith of Abu Umamah in Sunan Abi Dawud (1496). Others say 'La ilaha illa anta subhanaka.' All of these are among the most powerful names for du'a.
wednesday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 2:255; Al-Asma' wa as-Sifat by al-Bayhaqi; Sharh Asma' Allah al-Husna by Ibn al-Qayyim

wednesday.title: Qadar — Belief in Divine Decree
wednesday.arabic_text: وَعِندَهُ مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا هُوَ
wednesday.english_text: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. (Quran 6:59)
wednesday.lesson:
Belief in Qadar (divine decree) is the sixth pillar of Iman. The four levels of Qadar are: (1) 'Ilm — Allah knew all things before creation, (2) Kitabah — everything was written in al-Lawh al-Mahfuz (the Preserved Tablet), (3) Mashee'ah — nothing happens except by Allah's will, (4) Khalq — Allah is the creator of all things including human actions.

Believing in Qadar brings two opposite fruits: gratitude in blessing (because it came from Allah) and patience in hardship (because it came from Allah). A corps member who doesn't get their preferred posting, faces health challenges, or encounters professional obstacles — Qadar gives that person peace.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: If everything is decreed, why should I put in effort?
A: This is a misunderstanding of Qadar. The decree includes both your efforts AND the outcome. The Prophet said: 'Work, for everyone is facilitated for what they were created for.' (Sahih al-Bukhari 4945). Taking means is part of the decree — abandoning effort and calling it tawakkul is laziness.
wednesday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 8 (Hadith of Jibril); Kitab al-Iman by Ibn Mandah; Sharh al-Aqeedah al-Tahawiyyah by Ibn Abi al-Izz al-Hanafi

thursday.title: Fiqh of Debt — Rights and Responsibilities
thursday.arabic_text: نَفْسُ الْمُؤْمِنِ مُعَلَّقَةٌ بِدَيْنِهِ حَتَّى يُقْضَى عَنْهُ
thursday.english_text: The soul of the believer is suspended by his debt until it is paid off.
thursday.lesson:
Debt is a serious matter in Islam. The Prophet refused to pray Janazah (funeral prayer) over someone who died with outstanding debt until a companion agreed to pay it off. This does not mean debt is haram — the Prophet himself borrowed — but it means debt carries a heavy responsibility. Pay your debts promptly, keep records, and do not borrow what you cannot repay.

For corps members: Avoid debt traps during service year. Monthly allowances can tempt borrowing. The rule: do not borrow except in necessity, intend to repay, and repay as quickly as possible.
thursday.extra_notes:
Q: What about interest-bearing loans (riba) from banks or cooperatives?
A: Riba (interest) is absolutely prohibited in Islam — one of the most severely condemned sins in the Quran (2:275-279). Even small riba-based loans should be avoided. Seek interest-free loans from family, friends, or Islamic microfinance institutions. If you are already in a riba-based debt, repay it as quickly as possible without taking on new interest-bearing obligations.
thursday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 1078; Musnad Ahmad; Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli, Vol. 5

thursday.title: Fiqh of Ghusl — Mandatory Bath
thursday.arabic_text: وَإِن كُنتُمْ جُنُبًا فَاطَّهَّرُوا
thursday.english_text: And if you are in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity), then purify yourselves. (Quran 5:6)
thursday.lesson:
Ghusl (full ritual bath) becomes mandatory in five situations: sexual intercourse, ejaculation, end of menstruation, end of postnatal bleeding, and death (performed by others). The minimum valid ghusl consists of: intention, removing all impurity, and ensuring water reaches all parts of the body including under the hair roots. The Sunnah ghusl adds: washing the hands, private parts, performing wudu, and washing the whole body three times.

Without ghusl in the required circumstances, Salah, touching the Quran, and Tawaf are not valid.
thursday.extra_notes:
Q: Can I pray or fast while in a state of janabah if I haven't been able to perform ghusl?
A: For prayer — no, ghusl must be performed first unless water is unavailable (use tayammum). For fasting — yes, the fast is valid even if ghusl is delayed until after Fajr, as long as the ghusl is performed before prayer. The Prophet sometimes woke up in a state of janabah in Ramadan and completed his fast after performing ghusl.
thursday.source: Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq, Vol. 1; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah; Al-Fiqh 'ala al-Madhahib al-Arba'ah by al-Jaziri

friday.title: Going Early to Jumu'ah — The Reward of Each Hour
friday.arabic_text: مَنِ اغْتَسَلَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ غُسْلَ الْجَنَابَةِ ثُمَّ رَاحَ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَرَّبَ بَدَنَةً
friday.english_text: Whoever performs ghusl on Friday like the ghusl of janabah, then goes early to the masjid — it is as if he sacrificed a camel.
friday.lesson: The scholars explain that the reward decreases with each subsequent hour of arrival: first hour (camel), second hour (cow), third hour (ram), fourth hour (chicken), fifth hour (egg). The earlier you arrive, the greater the reward. For many corps members, the temptation to arrive late for Jumu'ah is real. This hadith tells you exactly what you lose with every minute of delay.
friday.extra_notes:
Etiquette inside the masjid while waiting for Jumu'ah:
- Pray nafl prayers until the imam ascends the minbar
- Read Quran, especially Surah al-Kahf
- Make dhikr and istighfar
- Do NOT step over people to get to the front row
- Do NOT speak during the khutbah
- Do NOT play with your phone
friday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 881; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 850; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah

friday.title: Friday Azkar — Du'a for Steadfastness
friday.arabic_text: يَا مُقَلِّبَ الْقُلُوبِ ثَبِّتْ قَلْبِي عَلَى دِينِكَ
friday.english_text: O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.
friday.transliteration: Ya muqallibal-quloob thabbit qalbi 'ala deenik.
friday.benefits: The Prophet made this du'a frequently. When Umm Salamah asked why, he said: 'There is no human being except that his heart is between two of Allah's fingers. Whomever He wills, He keeps firm, and whomever He wills, He causes to deviate.' This du'a is the acknowledgment that our hearts are in Allah's hands — and Friday, the day of renewal, is the best day to ask for firmness. A corps member surrounded by social pressure and temptation must make this du'a daily.
friday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 2140 (Hasan Sahih); Musnad Ahmad; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

saturday.title: Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf (RA) — Wealth as a Tool for Islam
saturday.arabic_text: بَشِّرْ أَصْحَابَ الثَّرْوَةِ بِالْكَدِّ الشَّدِيدِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِلَّا مَنْ أَنْفَقَهَا يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا
saturday.english_text: Give glad tidings to the wealthy of a difficult reckoning on the Day of Resurrection — except those who spent freely in all directions.
saturday.lesson:
Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf was one of the wealthiest companions of the Prophet and one of the ten promised Paradise. When he migrated to Madinah with nothing, an Ansari companion offered to share everything. Abdur-Rahman politely declined, asking only to be shown the marketplace. Within months, he had established a thriving business from scratch through his work ethic and Allah's blessings.

He gave enormous amounts of wealth in the way of Allah — including 700 camels loaded with trade goods in a single donation. Yet he was known for weeping, fearing that his wealth would slow him into Jannah.

Lesson: Work hard, earn lawfully, but do not let wealth imprison your heart. Use your professional skills — even as a corps member — to build financial literacy and the habit of giving.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 2048; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi; Usud al-Ghabah by Ibn al-Athir

saturday.title: Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) — The Scholar of Inheritance and Quran
saturday.arabic_text: أَعْلَمُكُمْ بِالْفَرَائِضِ زَيْدُ بْنُ ثَابِتٍ
saturday.english_text: The most knowledgeable of you in matters of inheritance is Zayd ibn Thabit.
saturday.lesson:
Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) was just thirteen years old when he first presented himself to serve the Prophet at the Battle of Badr — but was sent back due to his young age. He did not give up. He memorized the entire Quran, learned the Hebrew and Syriac languages at the Prophet's request, became the Prophet's primary scribe, and later led the committee that compiled the Quran into a single book under Abu Bakr and Uthman.

Lesson: Youth is not a disqualification. Zayd's story tells every young corps member: Develop specialist skills, embrace learning, and make yourself indispensable through knowledge — not connections.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 4986; Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 2907; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi

sunday.title: Ayyub (AS) — The Ultimate Test of Patience
sunday.arabic_text: وَأَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ
sunday.english_text: And Ayyub, when he called to his Lord: Adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. (Quran 21:83)
sunday.lesson:
Ayyub (AS) was afflicted with severe illness, loss of wealth, loss of children, and social isolation for eighteen years (some narrations say more). His wife served him faithfully throughout. Yet he never lost his gratitude or his trust in Allah. His supplication was not a complaint — it was an expression of need, followed by acknowledgment of Allah's mercy.

Allah restored everything: health, wealth, children, and honor. The Quran preserves his story as the model of sabr (patience) in adversity. For a corps member facing health issues, homesickness, financial strain, or professional setbacks: make Ayyub's du'a your companion.
sunday.source: Quran 21:83-84; Quran 38:41-44; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-Anbiya; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: The Story of Qarun — Wealth Without Gratitude
sunday.arabic_text: إِنَّ قَارُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ
sunday.english_text: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa, but he was insolent toward them. (Quran 28:76)
sunday.lesson:
Qarun was given such wealth that its keys alone required a group of strong men to carry. When advised to spend in the way of Allah, he declared: 'I was given this because of knowledge I possess.' He forgot the Source of his blessings. Allah caused the earth to swallow him, his wealth, and his home entirely.

The Quran preserves this story as a warning against 'innas-man ataahu Allahu' (the person to whom Allah gave) who forgets that the giving was from Allah. Every professional achievement, every financial gain, every talent a corps member possesses — these are from Allah. Attribute them correctly and use them correctly.
sunday.source: Quran 28:76-82; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-Qasas; Tafsir as-Sa'di, Surah al-Qasas

monday.title: Hadith on Smiling as Charity
monday.arabic_text: تَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ
monday.english_text: Your smile in the face of your brother is charity.
monday.transliteration: Tabasumuka fi wajhi akhika laka sadaqah.
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Jami' al-Tirmidhi (1956), classified as Hasan Sahih.
monday.lesson: Charity is not only financial. Every act of goodness to another person is sadaqah. A smile, a kind word, guiding someone who is lost, removing harm from a path, showing your teeth in joy to a fellow Muslim — all of these are documented acts of worship. The corps member who cannot give money can give smiles, and that too earns reward.
monday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 1956; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Charity; Sharh Riyad as-Salihin by Shaykh Ibn al-'Uthaymeen

monday.title: Hadith on the Neighbor
monday.arabic_text: مَا زَالَ جِبْرِيلُ يُوصِينِي بِالْجَارِ حَتَّى ظَنَنْتُ أَنَّهُ سَيُوَرِّثُهُ
monday.english_text: Jibreel kept advising me about the neighbor until I thought he would make him an heir.
monday.transliteration: Ma zaala jibreelu yooseeni bil-jaar hatta dhanantu annahu sa-yuwarrithuh.
monday.chain_of_narration: Aisha (RA) and Ibn Umar (RA) — narrated through multiple chains
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Aisha and Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them). Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (6014) and Sahih Muslim (2624).
monday.lesson: The rights of neighbors in Islam are extraordinarily emphasized. In a new posting, your neighbors are among your most important relationships. Greet them, share food with them, do not harm them with noise or waste, check on them when they are sick, and do not ignore their needs. Being a good neighbor is one of the clearest signs of Islamic character to a non-Muslim community.
monday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6014; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2624; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Neighbors

tuesday.title: Du'a for Entering the Toilet
tuesday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْخُبُثِ وَالْخَبَائِثِ
tuesday.english_text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from male and female evil spirits.
tuesday.transliteration: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-khubuthi wal-khaba'ith.
tuesday.benefits: The Prophet instructed this du'a before entering the toilet, with the left foot first. Toilets in Islamic theology are places where impure spirits (shayateen) congregate. The du'a places a barrier of divine protection around the believer. It takes one second to say — but marks the Muslim as conscious of Allah even in the most private moments.
tuesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 142; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 375; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

tuesday.title: Du'a After Completing Wudu
tuesday.arabic_text: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَّا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ، اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْنِي مِنَ التَّوَّابِينَ وَاجْعَلْنِي مِنَ الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ
tuesday.english_text: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. O Allah, make me of those who repent constantly and make me of those who purify themselves.
tuesday.transliteration: Ashhadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa rasuluh. Allahumma-j'alni minat-tawwabeen waj'alni minal-mutatahhireen.
tuesday.benefits: Whoever says this after wudu, all eight gates of Paradise are opened for them and they may enter through whichever they wish. (Sahih Muslim). Such an enormous reward for a few seconds of remembrance after a purification that was already obligatory. Stack your worship — follow every wudu with this dhikr.
tuesday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 234; Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 170; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

wednesday.title: Du'a Is Worship — The Core of Ibadah
wednesday.arabic_text: وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِي سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ
wednesday.english_text: And your Lord said: Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell in humiliation. (Quran 40:60)
wednesday.lesson: Du'a is described as 'the essence of worship' (Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3371). When you make du'a, you are practicing Tawheed in the most direct way — acknowledging that only Allah can answer, provide, guide, and protect. Not making du'a — out of arrogance, despair, or forgetfulness — is itself a sin. The believer makes du'a in joy and hardship, in abundance and scarcity.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Conditions for du'a to be answered:
1. Eat and earn from halal sources
2. Have certainty that Allah will answer
3. Do not be hasty in expecting the answer
4. Avoid making du'a against yourself, your family, or your wealth in anger
5. Times of greatest response: last third of the night, between adhan and iqamah, in sujud, on Fridays before Maghrib, when fasting, while traveling

Q: Why are some du'as not answered immediately?
A: The Prophet said Allah either grants the du'a, defers it to remove an equivalent evil, or stores it as reward for the Hereafter. (Musnad Ahmad). Every du'a is answered — just not always in the form expected.
wednesday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 40:60; Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 3371; Al-Wabil as-Sayyib by Ibn al-Qayyim

wednesday.title: Tawbah — The Door That Never Closes
wednesday.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقْبَلُ تَوْبَةَ الْعَبْدِ مَا لَمْ يُغَرْغِرْ
wednesday.english_text: Indeed, Allah accepts the repentance of a servant as long as the soul has not reached the throat (at death).
wednesday.lesson:
Tawbah (repentance) is one of the greatest gifts of Tawheed — the direct connection between the servant and Allah without any intermediary. No matter how great the sin — except shirk, which is forgiven with sincere tawbah while alive — Allah accepts repentance that is sincere. The Prophet said: 'Allah stretches out His hand at night to receive the repentance of those who sinned during the day, and He stretches out His hand during the day to receive the repentance of those who sinned at night.' (Sahih Muslim 2759).

For corps members who have fallen into sin during their service year — the door of tawbah is open. Do not let shame prevent you from returning to Allah.
wednesday.extra_notes:
The four conditions of valid tawbah:
1. Stop the sin immediately
2. Genuine remorse for having done it
3. Firm resolve never to return to it
4. If the sin involved another person's rights: make restitution or seek their forgiveness
wednesday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 3537; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2759; Madarij as-Salikin by Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyyah

thursday.title: Fiqh of Salat al-Musafir — Prayer While Travelling
thursday.arabic_text: لَيْسَ فِي السَّفَرِ إِثْمٌ أَنْ تُقَصِّرَ الصَّلَاةَ
thursday.english_text: There is no sin in shortening the prayer during travel.
thursday.lesson:
A traveler (musafir) may shorten four-rak'ah prayers (Dhuhr, Asr, Isha) to two rak'ahs. The travel distance for this concession is approximately 80 km (48 miles) according to the majority. The traveler may also combine Dhuhr with Asr and Maghrib with Isha. This dispensation applies as long as you have not formed the intention to settle in a location for more than four days (Shafi'i/Hanbali) or fifteen days (Hanafi/Maliki).

For corps members traveling to their posting location, attending inter-state CDS events, or going on field trips — they qualify as travelers and may use these concessions.
thursday.extra_notes:
Q: Once I arrive at my posting location for service year, am I still a traveler?
A: No. Once you establish residence at your PPA for the duration of the service year, you are a resident (muqim) and pray in full. The Sunnah is to pray full prayers at your place of residence.

Q: What if I return home to my family state for a visit?
A: You are a traveler during the journey and may shorten. Once home, you are a resident again.
thursday.source: Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq, Vol. 1; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah; Bidayat al-Mujtahid by Ibn Rushd

thursday.title: Fiqh of Amanah — Trustworthiness in Professional Life
thursday.arabic_text: أَدِّ الْأَمَانَةَ إِلَى مَنِ ائْتَمَنَكَ
thursday.english_text: Fulfill the trust of whoever has entrusted you.
thursday.lesson:
Amanah (trustworthiness) is not just about not stealing. It includes: fulfilling your work obligations honestly, accurate timekeeping, completing assigned tasks to the best of your ability, not using workplace resources for personal gain, and maintaining confidentiality of sensitive information. The Prophet identified betrayal of amanah as one of the signs of hypocrisy.

As a corps member, your employer, community, and the NYSC have placed trust in you. Your Islamic duty is to honor that trust fully — regardless of whether anyone is watching.
thursday.extra_notes:
Q: My supervisor at my PPA asks me to sign attendance for days I was absent. Is this allowed?
A: No. This is a betrayal of amanah — it constitutes fraud and bearing false witness. Politely decline and if pressured, consult MCAN leadership or escalate through proper NYSC channels. A small act of integrity protects your heart and your rizq.
thursday.source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 3534; Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 33 (signs of hypocrisy); Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli

friday.title: The Two Rak'ahs Before Jumu'ah — Tahiyyat al-Masjid
friday.arabic_text: إِذَا جَاءَ أَحَدُكُمُ الْمَسْجِدَ فَلَا يَجْلِسْ حَتَّى يَرْكَعَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ
friday.english_text: When one of you comes to the mosque, let him not sit until he has prayed two rak'ahs.
friday.lesson: Tahiyyat al-Masjid (greeting of the mosque) is two rak'ahs prayed upon entering the masjid before sitting. It is Sunnah Mu'akkadah. On Friday, arriving early and praying multiple nafl prayers before the Jumu'ah multiplies reward. The Prophet once stopped a man mid-khutbah to tell him to go pray two rak'ahs — such is the importance of this practice. Make arriving early enough to pray nafl a fixed Friday habit.
friday.extra_notes:
Nafl prayers on Friday:
- Four rak'ahs before Jumu'ah (reported from some scholars as recommended)
- Four rak'ahs after Jumu'ah OR two rak'ahs if prayed at home (Sahih Muslim, Hadith 882)
- These do not replace the Jumu'ah itself but surround it with additional worship
friday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 1163; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 714; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah

friday.title: Friday Azkar — Du'a for Parents
friday.arabic_text: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ
friday.english_text: My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my home as a believer, and the believing men and believing women. (Quran 71:28)
friday.transliteration: Rabbi-ghfir lee wa liwalidayya wa liman dakhala baytiya mu'minan wa lil-mu'mineena wal-mu'minat.
friday.benefits: This is the du'a of Nuh (AS) — who made it after centuries of calling his people. It encompasses yourself, your parents, your household, and the entire Muslim Ummah. On Friday — the day of heightened acceptance of du'a — this supplication is especially powerful. A corps member far from home should make this du'a in the final Friday hour for their parents.
friday.source: Quran 71:28; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Nuh; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

saturday.title: Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib (RA) — The Lion of Allah
saturday.arabic_text: سَيِّدُ الشُّهَدَاءِ حَمْزَةُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ
saturday.english_text: The master of the martyrs is Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib.
saturday.lesson:
Hamzah was the Prophet's uncle and one of the most powerful warriors in Arabia. His conversion to Islam gave the early Muslim community a feeling of strength and honor. He was killed at the Battle of Uhud by a spear thrown by a hired killer, Wahshi, and his body was mutilated by Hind bint Utbah. Yet the Prophet (who wept over Hamzah more than any other martyred companion) forgave those who did it.

Hamzah is called Asadullah (Lion of Allah) and Sayyid ash-Shuhada (Master of the Martyrs). He was buried where he fell on the hill of Uhud.

Lesson: Courage and sacrifice in the way of Allah — even if unwitnessed by anyone but Allah — carries the highest honor. A Muslim corps member who stands firm in their Islamic principles under social pressure is practicing a form of that same courage.
saturday.source: Mustadrak al-Hakim; Musnad Ahmad; As-Seerah an-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham; Sahih al-Bukhari, references to Battle of Uhud

saturday.title: Zaynab bint Muhammad (RA) — Faithfulness in Trial
saturday.arabic_text: وَاللَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَى زَيْنَبَ إِلَّا خَيْرًا
saturday.english_text: By Allah, we have never known of Zaynab except good.
saturday.lesson:
Zaynab (RA), the Prophet's eldest daughter, was married to Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi', a Makkan who was not yet Muslim at the time of revelation. When Abu al-As was captured at the Battle of Badr, Zaynab sent her dowry necklace as ransom from Makkah — and the Prophet, moved by the sight of Khadijah's necklace, had him released on condition he send Zaynab to Madinah. Later, Abu al-As embraced Islam and was reunited with Zaynab, who died shortly after.

Lesson: Faith is tested through the deepest human relationships. Zaynab's patience through separation from her husband, her loyalty to both her father and her marriage vows, and her quiet dignity through it all — are the mark of the Muslim woman who trusts Allah's plan above all else.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 2212; Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar; As-Seerah an-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham

sunday.title: Maryam (AS) — Purity, Trust, and the Miracle of Isa
sunday.arabic_text: إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِالرَّحْمَٰنِ مِنكَ إِن كُنتَ تَقِيًّا
sunday.english_text: She said: Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you fear Allah. (Quran 19:18)
sunday.lesson:
Maryam (AS) was chosen above all women of the world (Quran 3:42). She was a virgin who gave birth to Isa (Jesus, AS) by Allah's command alone. When she appeared with the baby and people accused her, she pointed to the infant — and the infant Isa spoke in defense of his mother from the cradle.

For the Muslim woman facing false accusations, social pressure, or unfair judgment: Maryam's story is your refuge. She relied entirely on Allah, sought refuge in Him when afraid, and trusted that His plan would vindicate her. It did — her name is immortalized in the Quran, the only woman to have a full surah named after her.
sunday.source: Quran 19:16-35; Quran 3:42-47; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Maryam; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: Isa ibn Maryam (AS) — The Miracle Prophet and His True Message
sunday.arabic_text: وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ لِّلسَّاعَةِ فَلَا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِهَا
sunday.english_text: And indeed, Isa will be a sign for the Hour, so be not in doubt about it. (Quran 43:61)
sunday.lesson:
Isa (AS) is one of the five greatest prophets (Ulul-'Azm). He was born of a virgin, spoke from the cradle, healed the sick, raised the dead — all by Allah's permission, not his own divinity. Islam honors him enormously while rejecting any claim of divinity. The Quran clarifies: 'He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor' (Quran 43:59).

Isa will return before the Day of Judgment, break the cross, kill the swine, and lead the believers against the Dajjal — affirming his role as a Muslim prophet until the end of time.

Lesson: Knowing the true story of Isa (AS) equips the corps member for respectful, informed dialogue with Christian colleagues about shared Abrahamic values while being clear about Islamic theology.
sunday.source: Quran 43:57-65; Quran 3:45-59; Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3448 (descent of Isa); Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Maryam

monday.title: Hadith on Keeping Family Ties (Silat al-Rahim)
monday.arabic_text: مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ وَيُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
monday.english_text: Whoever would like his provision to be expanded and his lifespan to be extended, let him maintain ties of kinship.
monday.transliteration: Man ahabba an yubsata lahu fi rizqihi wa yunsa'a lahu fi atharihi falyasil rahimah.
monday.chain_of_narration: Anas ibn Malik (RA) → Qatadah → Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (5986) and Sahih Muslim (2557).
monday.lesson: Maintaining family ties has a direct effect on rizq (provision) and lifespan. A corps member far from family must maintain contact: call parents regularly, check on siblings, send what you can financially, and make du'a for them. Cutting family ties is one of the most severe sins in Islam.
monday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 5986; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2557; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Silat al-Rahim

monday.title: Hadith on Obedience to Parents
monday.arabic_text: رِضَا الرَّبِّ فِي رِضَا الْوَالِدِ، وَسَخَطُ الرَّبِّ فِي سَخَطِ الْوَالِدِ
monday.english_text: The pleasure of the Lord is in the pleasure of the parent, and the anger of the Lord is in the anger of the parent.
monday.transliteration: Ridaar-rabbi fi ridaal-walid, wa sakhatuar-rabbi fi sakhatil-walid.
monday.chain_of_narration: Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As (RA) → multiple chains
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Jami' al-Tirmidhi (1899), classified as Sahih.
monday.lesson: Keeping your parents pleased is directly linked to keeping Allah pleased. The Muslim corps member calls home, respects parents' concerns about their posting, keeps them informed, and does not cause them unnecessary worry. Even parents who are not practicing Muslims deserve respect, kindness, and maintenance as long as they do not command disobedience to Allah.
monday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 1899; Al-Mustadrak by al-Hakim; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Parents

tuesday.title: Morning Dhikr — Allahumma bika asbahna
tuesday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا وَبِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا، وَبِكَ نَحْيَا وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ وَإِلَيْكَ النُّشُورُ
tuesday.english_text: O Allah, by You we enter the morning and by You we enter the evening, and by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection.
tuesday.transliteration: Allahumma bika asbahna wa bika amsayna, wa bika nahya wa bika namutu wa ilayka-n-nushur.
tuesday.benefits: This comprehensive morning dhikr acknowledges Allah's complete ownership over every moment — morning, evening, life, and death. It frames the entire day within divine sovereignty. A corps member who begins with this dhikr is reminded from the first conscious moment of their morning that everything they will do, experience, and accomplish is within Allah's hands.
tuesday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 3391 (Hasan); Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 5068; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

tuesday.title: Evening Dhikr — Allahumma bika amsayna
tuesday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا وَبِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا وَبِكَ نَحْيَا وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ
tuesday.english_text: O Allah, by You we enter the evening and by You we enter the morning, and by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the final return.
tuesday.transliteration: Allahumma bika amsayna wa bika asbahna, wa bika nahya wa bika namutu wa ilayka-l-maseer.
tuesday.benefits: This is the evening counterpart of the morning dhikr — said at Maghrib time. Note: the morning dhikr ends with 'an-nushur' (the resurrection/rising) reflecting the day ahead; the evening dhikr ends with 'al-maseer' (the final return) reflecting the night's approach to death. These paired dhikrs bracket the entire day in worship.
tuesday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 3391 (Hasan); Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 5069; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

wednesday.title: Al-Ghayb — Belief in the Unseen
wednesday.arabic_text: الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَاةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ
wednesday.english_text: Those who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided for them. (Quran 2:3)
wednesday.lesson: Belief in al-Ghayb (the unseen) is the first characteristic Allah mentions of the righteous in Surah al-Baqarah. This includes: belief in Allah's existence and attributes (which cannot be seen), angels, Jinn, the Barzakh (life after death before resurrection), Jannah and Jahannam, the events of the Day of Judgment, and divine decree. A Muslim whose Iman is rooted in al-Ghayb cannot be shaken by the materialist worldview that says 'only what is seen exists.'
wednesday.extra_notes: Real-life scenario: A colleague tells a corps member: 'You can't see Allah — why do you believe in Him?' The response: empirical science itself is built on unseen realities (gravity, electrons, emotions, consciousness). Belief in the unseen is rational when supported by revelation and reasoning. The Quran itself provides rational arguments for Allah's existence: the design argument (Quran 3:190), the cosmological argument (Quran 52:35), and the moral argument.
wednesday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 2:2-3; Al-Aqeedah al-Wasitiyyah by Ibn Taymiyyah; Sharh al-Aqeedah al-Tahawiyyah by Ibn Abi al-Izz

wednesday.title: The Angels — Belief and Reality
wednesday.arabic_text: آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِن رَّبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ
wednesday.english_text: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and so have the believers. All have believed in Allah, His angels... (Quran 2:285)
wednesday.lesson:
Belief in the angels is the second pillar of Iman. Angels are created from light, do not disobey Allah, have no free will as humans do, and are assigned specific duties. Among them: Jibreel (who brought revelation), Mika'il (responsible for rain and provisions), Israfeel (who will blow the Trumpet), Malik (keeper of Hellfire), Ridwan (keeper of Paradise), and the recording angels (Kiraman Katibin) who sit on your shoulders this very moment recording your deeds.

This last point is deeply practical: knowing that angels record every word, every act, every thought — is a constant reminder to the Muslim corps member to guard their behavior even when alone.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: Can angels appear in human form?
A: Yes. Jibreel appeared to the Prophet in human form on multiple occasions, most famously as the man in white in the Hadith of Jibril (Sahih Muslim 8). He also appeared to Maryam (AS) in human form (Quran 19:17).
wednesday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2996 (angels created from light); Al-Aqeedah al-Wasitiyyah by Ibn Taymiyyah; Sharh al-Aqeedah al-Tahawiyyah by Ibn Abi al-Izz

thursday.title: Fiqh of Giving Salam — Rules and Etiquette
thursday.arabic_text: لَا تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ حَتَّى تُؤْمِنُوا، وَلَا تُؤْمِنُوا حَتَّى تَحَابُّوا، أَوَلَا أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى شَيْءٍ إِذَا فَعَلْتُمُوهُ تَحَابَبْتُمْ؟ أَفْشُوا السَّلَامَ بَيْنَكُمْ
thursday.english_text: You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not tell you of something which, if you do it, will make you love one another? Spread the greeting of salam among yourselves.
thursday.lesson: Giving salam (assalamu alaykum) is a Sunnah, and responding to it is fard (obligatory). The one who gives first gets the greater reward. Rules include: the smaller greets the larger; the one on foot greets the one sitting; the smaller group greets the larger; the rider greets the pedestrian. Giving salam to non-Muslims: most scholars say you may give salam first to non-Muslims in contexts of necessity or good relations, responding to their greeting of peace is obligatory.
thursday.extra_notes:
Common mistakes:
- Saying 'salam' only (incomplete — the full salam is Sunnah)
- Not responding to salam — this is a sin
- Shaking hands with the right hand: recommended Sunnah
- Bowing when greeting: forbidden — this resembles non-Islamic customs
- Cheek-to-cheek greetings between non-mahrams: not permissible according to the majority
thursday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 54; Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq; Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli

thursday.title: Fiqh of Sadaqah — Voluntary Charity
thursday.arabic_text: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ
thursday.english_text: Charity never decreases wealth.
thursday.lesson:
Sadaqah (voluntary charity) is among the most rewarding acts in Islam. The Prophet said: 'Every day two angels descend and one says: O Allah, compensate the one who spends. The other says: O Allah, give loss to the one who withholds.' (Sahih al-Bukhari 1442). Sadaqah expiates sins, protects from calamity, extends lifespan, and multiplies provision — all established in authentic hadiths.

Forms of sadaqah: giving money, food sharing, physical assistance, teaching others, removing harm from paths, kind words, and even a smile. The corps member who cannot give large amounts should give consistently, even if small.
thursday.extra_notes: Sadaqah Jariyah (ongoing charity): The Prophet listed three acts whose reward continues after death: beneficial knowledge left behind, a righteous child who prays for the parent, and ongoing charity (waqf). A corps member who builds a small well, plants trees, or teaches community members Quran has planted Sadaqah Jariyah that earns reward long after their service year ends.
thursday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2588; Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 1442; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Sadaqah

friday.title: The First Jumu'ah in Madinah — Historical Context
friday.arabic_text: أَوَّلُ جُمُعَةٍ جُمِّعَتْ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ بَعْدَ جُمُعَةِ مَسْجِدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، جُمُعَةٌ بِجُوَاثَى
friday.english_text: The first Friday prayer held in Islam after that of the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah was the Friday prayer at Juwatha.
friday.lesson: The first Jumu'ah was performed by the Prophet shortly after the Hijrah to Madinah — before the Masjid an-Nabawi was even completed. The Muslim community, newly arrived and still building their society, did not delay the establishment of communal Friday prayer. This tells Muslim corps members: wherever you are posted, however new or unfamiliar — establish Jumu'ah. Seek your fellow Muslims, find a space, and pray together. The social act of Jumu'ah is itself a foundation of community.
friday.extra_notes:
What constitutes a valid Jumu'ah:
- Minimum number: scholars differ (3, 12, 40 people); the Hanbali minimum is three including the imam
- The prayer: two rak'ahs led by an imam after two khutbahs
- Location: traditionally in a town (misr); contemporary scholars allow Jumu'ah wherever Muslims gather regularly
- Time: begins at Dhuhr time and ends before Asr
friday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 892; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah; Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq

friday.title: Friday Azkar — Du'a for Protection of Deen
friday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الثَّبَاتَ فِي الْأَمْرِ، وَالْعَزِيمَةَ عَلَى الرُّشْدِ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ شُكْرَ نِعْمَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ حُسْنَ عِبَادَتِكَ
friday.english_text: O Allah, I ask You for firmness in all matters, and determination to follow the right path; I ask You for gratitude for Your blessings; and I ask You for excellence in Your worship.
friday.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'alukas-thabata fil-amr, wal-'azeemata 'alar-rushd, wa as'aluka shukra ni'matik, wa as'aluka husna 'ibadatik.
friday.benefits: This du'a from the collection of the Prophet covers four comprehensive requests: firm commitment, righteous determination, gratitude, and excellence in worship. On Friday — the day of renewal — it is the perfect re-commitment of the Muslim to their deen. It asks not for worldly things but for the qualities that make all worldly things meaningful.
friday.source: Musnad Ahmad, Hadith 22428; Sunan an-Nasa'i, Hadith 1304; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

saturday.title: Abu Hurayrah (RA) — The Greatest Hadith Narrator
saturday.arabic_text: لَوْلَا أَنِّي أَخْشَى أَنْ يَقُولَ النَّاسُ يُكْثِرُ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ
saturday.english_text: Were it not that I fear people would say Abu Hurayrah narrates too much...
saturday.lesson:
Abu Hurayrah embraced Islam in the seventh year after Hijrah — late in the Prophet's life — yet he narrated over 5,000 hadith, more than any other companion. How? He stayed permanently with the Prophet, never leaving for trade or farming, dedicating all his time to memorizing the Prophet's words. He was poor, hungry, and once fainted from starvation in the mosque — yet he stayed.

The Prophet prayed for him: 'O Allah, make Your servant here (Abu Hurayrah) beloved to the believers and make the believers beloved to him.' Muslim scholars testify that this du'a was answered — no companion is more beloved across the Muslim world.

Lesson: Total dedication to a worthy cause transforms poverty into legacy. What are you dedicating yourself to?
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 5634; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi; Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar

saturday.title: Umm Salamah (RA) — Wisdom and Counsel at the Highest Level
saturday.arabic_text: كَانَتْ مِنْ أَعْقَلِ النِّسَاءِ
saturday.english_text: She was among the most intelligent of women.
saturday.lesson:
Umm Salamah Hind bint Abi Umayyah (RA) was widowed during the migration to Abyssinia and later emigrated to Madinah with her children. After her husband Abu Salamah died from a battle wound, the Prophet himself proposed to her — and she accepted. She became one of the most respected of the Mothers of the Believers.

Her most famous moment came at the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah when the Prophet's companions were reluctant to comply with its seemingly unfavorable terms. Umm Salamah advised the Prophet: silently begin the rituals yourself — the companions will follow. He did exactly that, and they all followed without a word.

Lesson: The Muslim woman's wisdom and counsel has shaped history from the very beginning of Islam. Do not underestimate the power of wise counsel at the right moment.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 2731-2732 (Treaty of Hudaybiyyah); Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi

sunday.title: Dhul-Qarnayn — Justice, Power, and Gratitude
sunday.arabic_text: قَالَ هَٰذَا رَحْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّي
sunday.english_text: He said: This is a mercy from my Lord. (Quran 18:98)
sunday.lesson:
Dhul-Qarnayn (the man of two horns) was a righteous king who traveled to the East and West and the barriers between nations. When he built the wall between the people and Ya'juj and Ma'juj (Gog and Magog), the people offered him payment. He refused, attributing everything to his Lord.

Three qualities defined Dhul-Qarnayn: justice (he punished the wrongdoer and honored the righteous), power (he had the means to achieve great things), and gratitude (he credited Allah alone for his abilities). The corps member in authority — however small — should embody these three qualities.
sunday.source: Quran 18:83-98; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-Kahf; Tafsir as-Sa'di, Surah al-Kahf

sunday.title: The Story of the Two Gardens — Wealth and Arrogance
sunday.arabic_text: وَلَوْلَا إِذْ دَخَلْتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلْتَ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
sunday.english_text: And why did you not, when you entered your garden, say: What Allah wills will occur; there is no power except with Allah? (Quran 18:39)
sunday.lesson:
This Quranic story tells of a wealthy man with two magnificent gardens who was reminded by his believing companion to say 'Masha'Allah, la quwwata illa billah' (What Allah wills; there is no power except with Allah). He refused, claiming his wealth was due to his own merit and that it would never perish. His gardens were destroyed overnight.

For corps members who receive good postings, earn promotions, or find success in their projects: attribute everything to Allah. The phrase 'Masha'Allah' is not superstition — it is Tawheed in the moment of blessing. Acknowledging Allah's will in prosperity is the armor against its sudden loss.
sunday.source: Quran 18:32-44; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-Kahf; Tafsir as-Sa'di, Surah al-Kahf

monday.title: Hadith on the Sanctity of Muslim Blood
monday.arabic_text: كُلُّ الْمُسْلِمِ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِ حَرَامٌ: دَمُهُ وَمَالُهُ وَعِرْضُهُ
monday.english_text: Every Muslim to another Muslim is sacred: his blood, his wealth, and his honor.
monday.transliteration: Kullul-muslimi 'alal-muslimi haraam: damuhu wa maluhu wa 'irduhu.
monday.chain_of_narration: Abu Hurayrah (RA) → multiple chains including Sahih Muslim
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih Muslim (2564).
monday.lesson: Three things are inviolable regarding every Muslim: their life, their wealth, and their reputation. Harming any of these without right is a major sin. For corps members: do not spread rumors about colleagues, do not steal even small items, do not bully or physically intimidate anyone. The prohibition covers all three dimensions of harm.
monday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2564; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Forbidden Acts; Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 1927

monday.title: Hadith on Envy (Hasad)
monday.arabic_text: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْحَسَدَ فَإِنَّ الْحَسَدَ يَأْكُلُ الْحَسَنَاتِ كَمَا تَأْكُلُ النَّارُ الْحَطَبَ
monday.english_text: Beware of envy, for envy consumes good deeds just as fire consumes wood.
monday.transliteration: Iyyakum wal-hasad, fa-innal-hasada ya'kulul-hasanati kama ta'kulan-naru-l-hatab.
monday.chain_of_narration: Abu Hurayrah (RA) → narrated in Sunan Abi Dawud
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sunan Abi Dawud (4903), classified as Hasan.
monday.lesson: Hasad is wishing that a blessing be removed from another person. It devours good deeds. Ghubta (admiring someone's blessings and wishing for something similar for yourself, without wishing it removed from them) is permissible. When you see a fellow corps member succeed, check your heart: do you want what they have, or do you want them to lose it? The first is human nature; the second is a sin.
monday.source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 4903; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Envy; Al-Fawa'id by Ibn al-Qayyim

tuesday.title: Du'a for Anxiety — Allahuma inni abduk
tuesday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي عَبْدُكَ، ابْنُ عَبْدِكَ، ابْنُ أَمَتِكَ، نَاصِيَتِي بِيَدِكَ، مَاضٍ فِيَّ حُكْمُكَ، عَدْلٌ فِيَّ قَضَاؤُكَ، أَسْأَلُكَ بِكُلِّ اسْمٍ هُوَ لَكَ، سَمَّيْتَ بِهِ نَفْسَكَ، أَوْ أَنْزَلْتَهُ فِي كِتَابِكَ، أَوْ عَلَّمْتَهُ أَحَدًا مِنْ خَلْقِكَ، أَوِ اسْتَأْثَرْتَ بِهِ فِي عِلْمِ الْغَيْبِ عِنْدَكَ، أَنْ تَجْعَلَ الْقُرْآنَ رَبِيعَ قَلْبِي، وَنُورَ صَدْرِي، وَجَلَاءَ حُزْنِي، وَذَهَابَ هَمِّي
tuesday.english_text: O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant, son of Your maidservant. My forelock is in Your hand. Your command over me is continual, and Your decree concerning me is just. I ask You by every name You have, by which You named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept in the knowledge of the unseen with You — to make the Quran the spring of my heart, the light of my chest, the removal of my grief, and the departure of my anxiety.
tuesday.transliteration: Allahumma inni 'abduk, ibnu 'abdik, ibnu amatik, nasiyati bi-yadik...
tuesday.benefits: The Prophet promised: 'Allah will remove his grief and sorrow and replace it with joy.' The companion asked: 'Should we learn it, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes, whoever hears it should learn it.' This is the prescribed cure for anxiety and depression from the Prophetic medicine. Every corps member experiencing hardship should memorize this du'a.
tuesday.source: Musnad Ahmad, Hadith 3712; Classified as Sahih by al-Albani; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

tuesday.title: Dhikr Before Sleep — Tasbeeh of Fatimah
tuesday.arabic_text: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ (٣٣) الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ (٣٣) اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ (٣٤)
tuesday.english_text: SubhanAllah (33 times), Alhamdulillah (33 times), Allahu Akbar (34 times).
tuesday.transliteration: SubhanAllah (33x), Alhamdulillah (33x), Allahu Akbar (34x).
tuesday.benefits: This is the Tasbeeh of Fatimah — given by the Prophet to his daughter when she asked for a servant due to the hardship of housework. He told her: 'Shall I not tell you of something better than a servant?' Then he taught her this. The Prophet said it is better for you than a servant.' Saying it before sleep gives you strength for the next day — physical and spiritual — better than any worldly assistance.
tuesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3705; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2727; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

wednesday.title: Al-Akhirah — Certainty of the Next Life
wednesday.arabic_text: وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوَانُ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ
wednesday.english_text: And indeed, the home of the Hereafter is the true life, if only they knew. (Quran 29:64)
wednesday.lesson:
The certainty of the Akhirah (Hereafter) is a pillar of Islamic theology that transforms how a Muslim approaches every situation. The Prophet described this world as a bridge, not a home. The Muslim who knows with certainty that this life is temporary and the next eternal will: make decisions differently, handle injustice with greater patience, resist temptation more effectively, and find meaning in even the most difficult circumstances.

For corps members: every project, every interaction, every private moment is being recorded for the Day of Reckoning. This awareness — not fear, but certainty — is the most powerful motivator for righteousness.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: How do we know the Hereafter is real if we cannot see it?
A: The same way we know of black holes, the big bang, or historical events — through reliable testimony and evidence. The Quran provides consistent, detailed descriptions of the Hereafter across 114 chapters. The Prophet described it with extraordinary detail in authenticated hadith. Hundreds of thousands of witnesses — the companions — attested to his truthfulness. The rational Muslim accepts the unseen through revelation verified by reason.
wednesday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 29:64; Al-Aqeedah al-Wasitiyyah by Ibn Taymiyyah; Kitab ar-Ruh by Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyyah

wednesday.title: The Books of Allah — Belief in Divine Revelation
wednesday.arabic_text: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ
wednesday.english_text: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Quran, and indeed, We will be its guardian. (Quran 15:9)
wednesday.lesson:
Belief in the Books of Allah is the third pillar of Iman. This includes: the Suhuf (scriptures) of Ibrahim and Musa, the Zabur (Psalms) of Dawud, the Injeel (Gospel) of Isa, and the Quran — the final and preserved revelation. Unlike previous scriptures which were distorted over time, Allah Himself guaranteed the preservation of the Quran. It remains unchanged in text and recitation from the time of revelation.

For corps members: The Quran is not merely a book for Ramadan or funerals. It is the living guide for every question of your service year, every ethical dilemma, every moment of doubt. Read it daily, even if just one page.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: Do Muslims believe the Bible and Torah are divinely revealed?
A: Yes — in their original forms, before human alteration. The Quran confirms that original scriptures were revealed but have been changed (Quran 2:79). Muslims respect these scriptures but follow the Quran as the final, preserved revelation.
wednesday.source: Al-Aqeedah al-Wasitiyyah by Ibn Taymiyyah; Sharh al-Aqeedah al-Tahawiyyah by Ibn Abi al-Izz; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 15:9

thursday.title: Fiqh of Commanding Good and Forbidding Evil — Al-Amr bil-Ma'ruf
thursday.arabic_text: كُنتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ تَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَتَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنكَرِ
thursday.english_text: You are the best nation produced for mankind: you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. (Quran 3:110)
thursday.lesson:
Commanding good and forbidding wrong (al-amr bil-ma'ruf wan-nahy 'anil-munkar) is a collective religious duty. The Prophet established three levels: change it with your hand (authority), speak against it (tongue), and hate it in your heart (minimum of faith). The level at which you intervene depends on your authority and what will cause less harm than good.

For corps members: You have the authority to speak up against obvious wrongs in your CDS group, community project, or PPA — corruption, cheating, injustice. But this must be done with wisdom, not recklessness.
thursday.extra_notes:
Q: When should I NOT speak up against a wrong?
A: When speaking will cause greater harm than silence (e.g., provoking violence or losing your ability to do any good at all). When you lack the authority or knowledge to address it correctly. The principle: weigh the mafsadah (harm) of speaking versus the maslahah (benefit). Scholars advise: private counsel before public correction; gentle before firm.
thursday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 3:110; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 49; Al-Amr bil-Ma'ruf wan-Nahy 'anil-Munkar by Ibn Taymiyyah

thursday.title: Fiqh of Visiting the Sick — Ziyarat al-Marid
thursday.arabic_text: عُودُوا الْمَرِيضَ وَاتَّبِعُوا الْجَنَائِزَ تُذَكِّرُكُمُ الْآخِرَةَ
thursday.english_text: Visit the sick and follow the funeral processions — they remind you of the Hereafter.
thursday.lesson: Visiting the sick is a right of the Muslim upon fellow Muslims and a Sunnah act that carries immense reward. The Prophet said: 'When a Muslim visits a sick Muslim, he is gathering the fruit of Paradise until he returns.' (Sahih Muslim 2568). For corps members: when a colleague or neighbor falls ill, visit them, make du'a for them, bring food if possible, and encourage them with positive words. This is both Sunnah and a powerful way to spread Islamic character in your community.
thursday.extra_notes:
Du'a for the sick:
'As'alullaha-l-'azeem, Rabbal-'arshil-'azeem an yashfiyak' — I ask Allah the Mighty, the Lord of the Mighty Throne, to heal you. (Seven times)
This du'a from the Sunnah is prescribed to be said seven times over the sick person.

Etiquette: Do not stay too long (causes fatigue), bring something if possible, speak words of comfort and remind them of Allah's mercy, avoid discussing depressing medical prognoses.
thursday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2568; Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 2087; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

friday.title: The Jumu'ah Prayer in Numbers — Facts Every Muslim Should Know
friday.arabic_text: إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ سَيِّدُ الْأَيَّامِ وَأَعْظَمُهَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ
friday.english_text: Friday is the master of days and the greatest of them in the sight of Allah.
friday.lesson:
Key facts about Jumu'ah every Muslim corps member should know:
1. Fard for every free, adult, sane, resident Muslim male
2. Missing 3 consecutive Jumu'ahs without excuse causes the heart to be sealed (Tirmidhi)
3. The Prophet said sins between one Jumu'ah and the next are expiated — provided major sins are avoided
4. Angels record those who come first to Jumu'ah by the hour
5. There is a hidden hour on Friday when du'a is guaranteed to be answered
6. Reading Surah al-Kahf on Friday brings light between the two Fridays
friday.extra_notes:
Jumu'ah exemptions:
- Travelers (though they may pray if it causes no inconvenience)
- Women (not obligatory but permitted)
- Sick people who cannot attend
- Slaves (classical ruling, not applicable today)
- Those in severe weather conditions preventing attendance

If you miss Jumu'ah: pray Dhuhr as four rak'ahs. This does not eliminate the sin of missing Jumu'ah without excuse, but fulfills the fardh of the midday prayer.
friday.source: Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith 1084; Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 500 (missing Jumu'ah); Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah

friday.title: Friday Azkar — Du'a Against Poverty and Humiliation
friday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ اكْفِنِي بِحَلَالِكَ عَنْ حَرَامِكَ، وَأَغْنِنِي بِفَضْلِكَ عَمَّنْ سِوَاكَ
friday.english_text: O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful so that I have no need of what You have made unlawful, and make me self-sufficient through Your grace so that I need no one besides You.
friday.transliteration: Allahummak-fini bihalaalika 'an haramik, wa aghnini bifadlika 'amman siwak.
friday.benefits: This du'a was taught by the Prophet to Ali ibn Abi Talib when he was experiencing financial difficulty. It asks for two profound gifts: freedom from the need to pursue haram means of income, and freedom from financial dependence on other people. For corps members facing financial pressure during their service year — this is the precise du'a for your condition.
friday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 3563 (Hasan Gharib); Musnad Ahmad; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

saturday.title: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) — The Archer of Islam
saturday.arabic_text: ارْمِ سَعْدُ، فِدَاكَ أَبِي وَأُمِّي
saturday.english_text: Shoot, Sa'd! May my father and mother be sacrificed for you.
saturday.lesson:
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) was among the first to embrace Islam and was the first person to shed blood in the way of Allah when he struck a polytheist who was harassing a group of Muslims. The Prophet dedicated both his parents as ransom for Sa'd — an honor he gave to no other companion in the same words.

Sa'd later led the Islamic armies to defeat the Persian Empire at the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah, opening Iraq to Islam. He is also known for his powerful and accepted du'a — the Prophet attested that his supplications were always answered.

Lesson: Specialization in a skill — whether archery in Sa'd's case or your professional expertise today — combined with faith, makes you an instrument of great change. Sa'd was not the most famous companion, but he was the most effective in his specific role.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3725; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2412; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi

saturday.title: Hafsah bint Umar (RA) — Keeper of the Quran
saturday.arabic_text: كَانَتْ حَافِظَةً لِلْقُرْآنِ
saturday.english_text: She was a preserver (hafizah) of the Quran.
saturday.lesson:
Hafsah bint Umar (RA) was the daughter of Umar ibn al-Khattab and one of the Mothers of the Believers. She was known for her lengthy fasts, her frequent night prayers, and her extraordinary memory. When Abu Bakr ordered the Quran to be compiled after the Battle of Yamama, the completed written copy was entrusted to Hafsah for safekeeping — making her the guardian of the written Quran until Uthman's standardization.

She passed away in Madinah around the year 41 AH, having served Islam through scholarship, worship, and the preservation of the Quran itself.

Lesson: The Muslim woman as keeper and preserver of sacred knowledge is not a modern aspiration — it is the original Islamic reality.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 4986 (collection of Quran); Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi

sunday.title: Hud (AS) — Courage Against a Mighty Nation
sunday.arabic_text: إِنِّي تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ رَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ
sunday.english_text: Indeed, I have put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord. (Quran 11:56)
sunday.lesson:
Hud (AS) was sent to the people of 'Ad — described as the most powerful people of their time, who said: 'Who is stronger than us?' (Quran 41:15). They were the tallest, most physically powerful civilization of their era. Hud preached to them patiently, warning them of destruction. When they mocked him and threatened him with their gods, Hud declared his complete tawakkul in Allah.

Allah sent upon them a furious wind that destroyed them utterly — leaving nothing but ruins. Their ruins are called Iram of the Pillars (Quran 89:7).

Lesson: No amount of worldly power, physical strength, or political influence protects a community from Allah's will when they persist in transgression. And no amount of worldly weakness can harm the person who places complete trust in Allah.
sunday.source: Quran 11:50-60; Quran 46:21-26; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Hud; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: Salih (AS) and the She-Camel of Allah
sunday.arabic_text: وَيَا قَوْمِ هَٰذِهِ نَاقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً
sunday.english_text: O my people, this is the she-camel of Allah, a sign for you. (Quran 11:64)
sunday.lesson:
Salih (AS) was sent to the Thamud, a powerful people who carved their homes in mountains. They demanded a sign — Allah caused a she-camel of miraculous origin to emerge from a rock. The camel was given its own watering day among their water sources. When the most wicked among them hamstrung and killed the camel in arrogant defiance, Salih warned them of three days remaining before punishment. On the fourth day, a mighty blast destroyed them.

Lesson: The signs of Allah are everywhere. When a community deliberately destroys what Allah has provided — natural resources, honesty, justice — they invite a reckoning. The Muslim corps member in a resource extraction or environmental project should remember the camel of Thamud.
sunday.source: Quran 11:61-68; Quran 91:13-15; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Hud; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

monday.title: Hadith on the Pen — Writing as Ibadah
monday.english_text: Preserve knowledge by writing it down.
monday.chain_of_narration: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (RA); authenticated in various collections
monday.reported_by: Attributed to the Prophet and narrated by Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As. Recorded in al-Mustadrak by al-Hakim (341) and other collections.
monday.lesson: Writing is an act of preserving knowledge — and by extension, an act of worship when the knowledge preserved is Islamic. The companions wrote down hadith, tafsir, and fiqh rulings to preserve them for future generations. As a corps member, keep a journal of the Islamic knowledge you are learning. Notes from khutbahs, from Quran recitation, from Islamic books — all of these are seeds of lasting benefit.
monday.source: Al-Mustadrak by al-Hakim, Vol. 1; authenticated in various hadith compilations; Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm wa Fadlih by Ibn Abd al-Barr

monday.title: Hadith on Consulting Others (Shura)
monday.arabic_text: مَا خَابَ مَنِ اسْتَخَارَ وَلَا نَدِمَ مَنِ اسْتَشَارَ
monday.english_text: One who performs Istikhara never fails, and one who consults others never regrets.
monday.transliteration: Ma khaaba manistaakhara wa la nadima man istashara.
monday.chain_of_narration: Anas ibn Malik (RA) → narrated through several chains
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat by al-Tabarani, classified as Hasan by some scholars.
monday.lesson: Shura (consultation) is a Quranic principle of governance and personal decision-making (Quran 42:38). Before making major decisions — career choices, personal commitments, project directions — consult those with relevant experience and wisdom. Combined with Istikhara (seeking Allah's guidance through prayer), this is the Islamic method of decision-making.
monday.source: Al-Mu'jam al-Awsat by al-Tabarani; Jami' al-Ulum wal-Hikam references to shura; Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh, Vol. 6

tuesday.title: Salat al-Istikhara — Seeking Allah's Guidance
tuesday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ، وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ الْعَظِيمِ
tuesday.english_text: O Allah, I seek Your guidance by Your knowledge, and I seek Your assistance by Your power, and I ask You of Your great bounty.
tuesday.transliteration: Allahumma inni astakheeruka bi-'ilmik, wa astaqdiruka bi-qudratik, wa as'aluka min fadlikal-'azeem...
tuesday.benefits: Salat al-Istikhara is the prescribed prayer for seeking guidance in matters of uncertainty. Two rak'ahs are prayed with the intention of istikhara, then this du'a is made mentioning the specific matter. The response comes through feelings of ease or difficulty in the heart, through circumstances, or through a dream — but the Muslim should proceed with what they feel inclined toward after the prayer, trusting Allah's guidance. Corps members facing uncertain decisions should use this regularly.
tuesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 1162 (full du'a); Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Istikhara; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

tuesday.title: Dhikr for Difficult Times — Hasbunallah
tuesday.arabic_text: حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ
tuesday.english_text: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.
tuesday.transliteration: Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal-wakeel.
tuesday.benefits: This was the statement of Ibrahim (AS) when he was thrown into fire, and the statement of the companions when they were told 'people have gathered against you, so fear them' (Quran 3:173). In both cases, it resulted in the fire becoming cool and the enemy retreating. This dhikr is for the moment when you feel overwhelmed by circumstances beyond your control. It does not deny the problem — it transcends it by acknowledging Allah as sufficient.
tuesday.source: Quran 3:173-174; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 3:173; Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 4563; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

wednesday.title: The Messengers — Belief in the Prophets
wednesday.arabic_text: آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِن رَّبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ
wednesday.english_text: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and so have the believers. All have believed in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers. (Quran 2:285)
wednesday.lesson:
Belief in all the Prophets and Messengers of Allah is the fourth pillar of Iman. Allah sent approximately 124,000 prophets (according to one hadith) and 315 messengers with specific laws. Of these, 25 are named in the Quran. We are required to: believe in all of them, honor all of them, not distinguish between them in terms of their prophethood (Quran 2:285), and follow the final one — Muhammad (peace be upon him).

Disbelieving in any prophet, including Isa or Musa, makes a person a non-Muslim. Islam's respect for all prophets is one of the most unique features of our faith.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: Is Jesus a prophet in Islam?
A: Yes — Isa ibn Maryam (AS) is one of the five greatest prophets in Islam (Ulul-'Azm), born of a virgin, given the Injeel, capable of miracles by Allah's permission. What Islam rejects is his divinity or that he died on the cross. The Quran states Allah raised him up (Quran 4:158).
wednesday.source: Al-Aqeedah al-Wasitiyyah by Ibn Taymiyyah; Sharh al-Aqeedah al-Tahawiyyah by Ibn Abi al-Izz; Musnad Ahmad, Hadith 22342 (number of prophets)

wednesday.title: The Day of Judgment — Yawm al-Qiyamah
wednesday.arabic_text: يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ مُّحْضَرًا وَمَا عَمِلَتْ مِن سُوءٍ
wednesday.english_text: On the Day every soul will find what it has done of good present before it, and what it has done of evil. (Quran 3:30)
wednesday.lesson:
Yawm al-Qiyamah (Day of Judgment) is the fifth pillar of Iman. Every human being will be resurrected from death and stand before Allah to account for every deed, word, and intention. The Quran describes it in extraordinary detail: the trumpet blasts, the resurrection, the gathering, the scales, the sirat (bridge over Hellfire), and the final destination in Jannah or Jahannam.

This belief is the ultimate accountability mechanism. The corps member who knows with certainty that they will stand before Allah for their treatment of colleagues, their honesty in work, and their use of time — has the most powerful motivation imaginable for righteous conduct.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Signs of the approaching Hour:
Minor signs include: widespread ignorance of religion, consumption of alcohol, widespread music, immorality, buildings competing in height, the spread of wealth. Major signs include: the Dajjal, descent of Isa, Ya'juj and Ma'juj, three landslides, the sun rising from the West. Many minor signs have already appeared.
wednesday.source: Kitab Ahwal al-Qiyamah by al-Qurtubi; Al-Aqeedah al-Wasitiyyah by Ibn Taymiyyah; Ahwal Yawm al-Qiyamah by Umar Sulayman al-Ashqar

thursday.title: Fiqh of the Quran — Touching, Recitation, and Etiquette
thursday.arabic_text: لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ
thursday.english_text: None shall touch it except the purified. (Quran 56:79)
thursday.lesson:
The majority of scholars (Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali) hold that touching the Quran requires wudu. Recitation from memory is permissible without wudu but not recommended in a state of major impurity (janabah). Menstruating women: scholars differ — the majority do not permit touching the Quran during menstruation, but many contemporary scholars allow it for students and teachers out of necessity.

Etiquette of the Quran: recite with tajweed, face the Qiblah if possible, begin with ta'awwudh (A'udhu billah) and Bismillah, recite with proper reflection (tadabbur), do not place the Quran on the floor or disrespect it in any way.
thursday.extra_notes:
Q: Can I read the Quran on my phone without wudu?
A: The majority of contemporary scholars permit reading Quran on a phone or tablet without wudu because the phone itself is not a Quran — it displays the text. However, it is recommended to maintain wudu when reciting out of reverence for the words of Allah.

Q: Is it permissible to recite Quran in a non-Arabic language?
A: The Quran must be recited in Arabic to count as Quran for the purpose of Salah and Tilawah reward. Translations are not Quran — they are interpretations of meaning.
thursday.source: Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli; Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq; Bidayat al-Mujtahid by Ibn Rushd

thursday.title: Fiqh of Dhikr and Du'a — When, How, and Conditions
thursday.arabic_text: وَاذْكُر رَّبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ تَضَرُّعًا وَخِيفَةً وَدُونَ الْجَهْرِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصَالِ
thursday.english_text: Remember your Lord within yourself in humility and in awe, without being loud in speech, in the mornings and evenings. (Quran 7:205)
thursday.lesson: Dhikr (remembrance of Allah) and du'a (supplication) are not confined to formal prayer times. They are the breath of the believer's spiritual life. Conditions for du'a to be more likely accepted: purity, facing the Qiblah, raising the hands, beginning with hamd and salawat, making du'a with certainty and urgency, not eating haram, and choosing the blessed times. Scholars note that dhikr in the heart (khafi) is superior to vocal dhikr in most contexts, though communal dhikr (halaqah) has its own place.
thursday.extra_notes:
Recommended times for du'a:
- Last third of the night (tahajjud time)
- During Sujud in Salah
- Between adhan and iqamah
- When fasting and at iftar
- On Fridays during the final hour
- During rainfall
- When traveling
- On the Day of Arafah (Dhul-Hijjah 9)
- On Laylat al-Qadr (odd nights of last 10 of Ramadan)
thursday.source: Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli; Al-Wabil as-Sayyib by Ibn al-Qayyim; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

friday.title: The Imam of Jumu'ah — Conditions and Responsibilities
friday.arabic_text: إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ الْإِمَامُ لِيُؤْتَمَّ بِهِ
friday.english_text: The imam is appointed to be followed.
friday.lesson:
The imam of Jumu'ah carries a significant responsibility: to lead the community in worship, to deliver a relevant and beneficial khutbah, and to represent Islamic values publicly. The conditions for a valid Jumu'ah imam include: being Muslim, male (for Jumu'ah specifically), adult, sane, and able to recite Quran correctly. The Sunnah is for the most knowledgeable in Islamic law to lead, then the best in Quran recitation, then the oldest in Islam.

For corps members who find themselves in locations where no knowledgeable imam is available: it is permitted for the most knowledgeable among the group to lead — even if he is a corps member. Establish the prayer; do not leave it because of perceived insufficiency.
friday.extra_notes: For MCAN CDS groups: Designating a religious officer (amir) who leads Friday prayers, organizes Islamic activities, and represents the Muslim corps members before NYSC authorities is a recommended organizational step. The Prophet said: 'When three people travel together, let them appoint one as their leader.' (Abu Dawud 2608)
friday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 722; Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah

friday.title: Friday Azkar — The Du'a of the Prophets in Distress
friday.arabic_text: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ
friday.english_text: There is no god but You. Glory be to You. Indeed I have been of the wrongdoers. So We responded to him and saved him from distress. (Quran 21:87-88)
friday.transliteration: La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu minadh-dhalimeen.
friday.benefits: This is Yunus's du'a from inside the whale — used here on Friday as the du'a of complete surrender. The Quran says Allah 'saved him from distress' as a direct response. The scholars say this du'a combines the three essential elements of tawbah and du'a: affirming Tawheed, glorifying Allah, and confessing fault. On Friday, in the final hour, make this du'a with complete sincerity for whatever matter is weighing on your heart.
friday.source: Quran 21:87-88; Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 3505 (Sahih); Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-Anbiya

saturday.title: Talhah ibn Ubaydillah (RA) — The Living Martyr
saturday.arabic_text: طَلْحَةُ مِمَّنْ قَضَى نَحْبَهُ
saturday.english_text: Talhah is among those who fulfilled their pledge.
saturday.lesson:
Talhah ibn Ubaydillah (RA) was one of the ten companions promised Paradise. At the Battle of Uhud, when the Prophet was in danger of being killed, Talhah used his own body as a shield — covering the Prophet with his hand and receiving over seventy wounds. His hand became permanently paralyzed from protecting the Prophet from a blow. The Prophet called him 'Talhah the Good' and 'Talhah the Generous.'

He was a wealthy man of Makkah who gave his entire fortune repeatedly in the way of Allah — once distributing 700,000 dirhams in a single day.

Lesson: True loyalty and love for the Prophet is demonstrated through action, sacrifice, and consistency — not just feeling. And wealth in the hands of a generous Muslim is a force for good that extends beyond a single lifetime.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3724; Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 3739; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi

saturday.title: Umm Sulaym bint Milhan (RA) — The Courageous Mother
saturday.arabic_text: دَخَلَ النَّبِيُّ عَلَى أُمِّ سُلَيْمٍ فَقَالَ مَا هَذَا؟ قَالَتْ سَيْفٌ أَشُدُّهُ
saturday.english_text: The Prophet entered upon Umm Sulaym (during a battle) and she said: It is a sword — I have it tied to me.
saturday.lesson:
Umm Sulaym (RA) was a woman of extraordinary courage, intelligence, and faith. When her first husband Malik ibn al-Nadr refused to embrace Islam, she refused to remain in the marriage — one of the early Muslim women to choose faith over comfort in the home. She later married Abu Talhah al-Ansari after he embraced Islam as her mahr (dowry).

When her son died, she showed remarkable composure, breaking the news to her husband with extraordinary wisdom and receiving the Prophet's du'a for a blessed replacement — which came in the form of their son Abdullah who became a scholar and father of ten Quran memorizers.

Lesson: The strength of a Muslim woman is not measured by comfort but by the depth of her faith in the most difficult moments.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 1301; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2144; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi

sunday.title: Shu'ayb (AS) — The Prophet of Business Ethics
sunday.arabic_text: وَلَا تَنقُصُوا الْمِكْيَالَ وَالْمِيزَانَ إِنِّي أَرَاكُم بِخَيْرٍ وَإِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ مُّحِيطٍ
sunday.english_text: And give full measure and weight, and do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth. (Quran 11:85)
sunday.lesson:
Shu'ayb (AS) was sent to the people of Madyan and Aykah, who were notorious for cheating in weights and measures in trade. His entire message centered on business ethics: honest scales, fair prices, and not defrauding customers. When they rejected him, they were destroyed by a thunderous blast.

For the Muslim corps member in any commercial, financial, or administrative role: business ethics is prophetic ethics. Giving full measure — doing your job completely and honestly — is the Sunnah of Shu'ayb and a direct command of the Quran.
sunday.source: Quran 11:84-95; Quran 7:85-93; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Hud; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: Lut (AS) — Standing Alone Against Community Immorality
sunday.arabic_text: قَالَ رَبِّ انصُرْنِي عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْمُفْسِدِينَ
sunday.english_text: He said: My Lord, support me against the corrupting people. (Quran 29:30)
sunday.lesson:
Lut (AS) lived among a people who had normalized a grave sexual transgression. He preached to them for years, standing alone in calling them to righteousness while his own wife sided with them. When the angels came in human form and the people surrounded his house with evil intent, Lut made du'a to Allah. Allah destroyed the entire settlement — and spared only Lut and his daughters.
