She was one of the earliest Muslim women to lead prayer in her own household — the Prophet appointed a muadhdhin for her and permitted her to lead the women and elderly men of her household.

Lesson: The Muslim woman who memorizes the Quran carries the most honored of all Islamic distinctions — one that the Prophet personally honored through his visits.
saturday.source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 591; Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar; Usud al-Ghabah by Ibn al-Athir

sunday.title: The People of Lut — Cities Destroyed for Transgression
sunday.arabic_text: فَلَمَّا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا جَعَلْنَا عَالِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا
sunday.english_text: And when Our command came, We made the highest part of it its lowest. (Quran 11:82)
sunday.lesson:
The five cities of Sodom and Gomorrah (the people of Lut) were destroyed by Allah's direct command — turned upside down and showered with stones — for their persistent transgression. The Quran mentions their destruction in at least eight places, and in each mention draws a moral: every community that persists in oppression and moral corruption after clear warning has appointed its own doom.

For a Muslim corps member: avoiding the sins that destroyed these communities is not cultural conservatism — it is direct Quranic instruction. And more broadly: the Quran's repeated reference to destroyed nations is a warning that history's moral arc bends toward justice — eventually.
sunday.source: Quran 11:77-83; Quran 7:80-84; Quran 26:160-175; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Hud; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: The Story of the Sabbath-Breakers — Consequences of Violating Allah's Commands
sunday.arabic_text: فَلَمَّا عَتَوْا عَن مَّا نُهُوا عَنْهُ قُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ
sunday.english_text: And when they exceeded the limits of what they had been forbidden from, We said to them: Be apes, despised. (Quran 7:166)
sunday.lesson:
A group from Bani Isra'il was prohibited from fishing on the Sabbath (Saturday). Fish would appear abundantly on Saturday and disappear on other days. Some began setting nets on Friday to catch fish that were technically caught on other days. When warned, they dismissed the concern. The result: Allah transformed those who violated the prohibition and scoffed at the warning.

Three groups: those who violated, those who remained silent and stopped warning (considering it hopeless), and those who continued to warn. Only the last group was saved.

Lesson: Religious prohibition-workarounds that technically comply while violating the spirit are condemned in the Quran. And the duty to speak up continues even when it seems hopeless.
sunday.source: Quran 7:163-166; Quran 2:65; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-A'raf; Tafsir as-Sa'di, Surah al-A'raf

monday.title: Hadith on Sincerity (Ikhlas)
monday.arabic_text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَأَمْوَالِكُمْ، وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ وَأَعْمَالِكُمْ
monday.english_text: Indeed Allah does not look at your forms or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
monday.transliteration: Innallaha la yanduru ila suwarikum wa amwalikum, wa lakin yanduru ila qulubikum wa a'malikum.
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih Muslim (2564).
monday.lesson: The divine evaluation of human beings is based entirely on the heart and action — not appearance, wealth, ethnicity, or position. In an NYSC environment where corps members may compare postings, allowances, and social status — this hadith is a powerful equalizer. The poorest corps member with a sincere heart outranks the richest one with a corrupted one in the only ledger that matters.
monday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2564; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Ikhlas; Sharh Sahih Muslim by Imam an-Nawawi

monday.title: Hadith on Leaving Doubtful Matters
monday.arabic_text: دَعْ مَا يَرِيبُكَ إِلَى مَا لَا يَرِيبُكَ
monday.english_text: Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.
monday.transliteration: Da' ma yareebuka ila ma la yareebuk.
monday.reported_by: Narrated by al-Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Jami' al-Tirmidhi (2518) and Sunan an-Nasa'i (5711), classified as Sahih.
monday.lesson: When in doubt about the permissibility of something — food, a business transaction, a social situation, a professional decision — the Islamic principle is to take the safe path. This does not mean paralysis in every decision, but when genuine doubt exists, err on the side of caution. The Prophet called this principle 'wara' (scrupulous caution) — one of the marks of the righteous.
monday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 2518; Sunan an-Nasa'i, Hadith 5711; Jami' al-Ulum wal-Hikam by Ibn Rajab, Hadith 11

tuesday.title: Morning Dhikr — Raditu billahi Rabba
tuesday.arabic_text: رَضِيتُ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا وَبِالإِسْلَامِ دِينًا وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيًّا
tuesday.english_text: I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, Islam as my religion, and Muhammad as my Prophet.
tuesday.transliteration: Raditu billahi Rabban wa bil-Islami dinan wa bi-Muhammadin nabiyyan.
tuesday.benefits: The Prophet said: 'Whoever says this three times in the morning and evening, it is a right upon Allah to please him on the Day of Resurrection.' (Sunan Abi Dawud 5072). This dhikr is a declaration of complete satisfaction with Allah's choices — your Lord, your religion, and your Prophet are not compromises or impositions; they are the objects of your deepest satisfaction. Begin every morning with this statement of contentment and watch how your day changes.
tuesday.source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 5072; Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 3389; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

tuesday.title: Dhikr for Protection from Shaytan — A'udhu bi kalimatillah
tuesday.arabic_text: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍ
tuesday.english_text: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from every devil and every poisonous creature and from every evil eye.
tuesday.transliteration: A'udhu bikalimatillahit-tammati min kulli shaytanin wa hammatin wa min kulli 'aynin lammah.
tuesday.benefits: This is the ruqyah (protective supplication) the Prophet recited over al-Hasan and al-Husayn, saying: 'Your forefather Ibrahim used to seek refuge with these words for Isma'il and Ishaq.' Reciting this for yourself, your children, or anyone in your care provides protection from shayateen, harmful creatures, and the evil eye — all by the authority of the perfect words of Allah.
tuesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3371; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

wednesday.title: Zuhd — Detachment from the World
wednesday.arabic_text: وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا مَتَاعُ الْغُرُورِ
wednesday.english_text: And what is the worldly life except the enjoyment of delusion. (Quran 3:185)
wednesday.lesson:
Zuhd (detachment from the world) does not mean poverty, withdrawal from society, or neglecting one's duties. Ibn al-Qayyim defined zuhd as: 'Leaving what does not benefit you in the Hereafter.' A person of zuhd may be wealthy but their heart is not attached to wealth. A person of zuhd works hard but is not crushed when they fail. The world is in their hand but not in their heart.

The Prophet compared the dunya (world) to a traveler's tree — you rest under it briefly, then continue the journey. The tree is real and useful, but you don't build your home in it.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: Doesn't Islam encourage working and earning?
A: Yes, absolutely. Islam encourages lawful work, building of skills, provision for family, and contributing to society. Zuhd is about the heart's attachment — not the hand's engagement. The difference: a person attached to the world feels devastated when they lose it; a person of zuhd feels grateful when they have it and patient when they lose it.
wednesday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 3:185; Al-Fawa'id by Ibn al-Qayyim; Uddat as-Sabirin by Ibn al-Qayyim

wednesday.title: The Akhirah — Jannah and Its Reality
wednesday.arabic_text: فِيهَا مَا تَشْتَهِيهِ الْأَنفُسُ وَتَلَذُّ الْأَعْيُنُ
wednesday.english_text: In it (Paradise) is whatever the souls desire and what delights the eyes. (Quran 43:71)
wednesday.lesson:
Jannah (Paradise) is described in the Quran and Sunnah in extraordinary sensory detail: rivers of water, milk, honey, and wine (non-intoxicating), fruits of every kind always in season, dwellings more beautiful than the human mind can conceive, garments of silk, and — above all — the pleasure of seeing Allah (Quran 75:22-23). The Prophet said the least of its inhabitants will think they have the most — because Allah's hospitality is beyond comparison.

For the Muslim corps member enduring hardship: keeping the reality of Jannah alive in the mind transforms every difficulty into a down payment. 'Are you patient for the span of the world in exchange for eternal Jannah?' — when framed this way, every sacrifice becomes obviously worth it.
wednesday.extra_notes: The greatest reward of Jannah: 'The believers will see their Lord with their own eyes, just as you see the full moon with no difficulty.' (Sahih al-Bukhari 806). All other pleasures of Jannah pale in comparison to seeing Allah. This is the ultimate goal of the Muslim life — and every act of worship in this world is a step toward that eternal vision.
wednesday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 43:71; Haadi al-Arwah ila Bilad al-Afrah by Ibn al-Qayyim; Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 806

thursday.title: Fiqh of Buying and Selling — Islamic Business Ethics
thursday.arabic_text: التَّاجِرُ الصَّدُوقُ الأَمِينُ مَعَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ وَالشُّهَدَاءِ
thursday.english_text: The truthful and trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful, and the martyrs.
thursday.lesson:
Islamic commerce is governed by clear ethical principles: no riba (interest), no gharar (excessive uncertainty in contracts), no tadlees (concealment of defects), no ihtikar (hoarding to inflate prices), full disclosure of defects, honest weighing, and honoring contracts. The honest merchant earns the company of prophets and martyrs on the Day of Judgment.

For corps members engaged in any form of trade or commerce during their service year: every business transaction is an opportunity for worship if conducted with the Prophet's standards of honesty.
thursday.extra_notes:
Common issues in business:
- Online sales: must disclose accurate descriptions; misleading product photos are fraudulent
- Group buying/cooperative: permissible if structured transparently
- Lending money to colleagues: avoid interest; if you lend, accept what is returned without addition
- Price negotiation: permissible and Sunnah; do not quote false prices to start negotiations
thursday.source: Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Hadith 1209; Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli; Halal and Haram in Islam by Yusuf al-Qaradawi

thursday.title: Fiqh of Istishara — Seeking Advice Before Decisions
thursday.arabic_text: وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ
thursday.english_text: And consult them in the matter. (Quran 3:159)
thursday.lesson:
Allah commanded the Prophet himself — the most guided of all humans — to consult his companions in important matters. This Quranic command establishes shura (consultation) as a fundamental principle of Islamic governance and personal decision-making. Ibn Atiyyah said: 'There is no Muslim who consults with those who have knowledge and piety except that Allah guides them to the best outcome.'

For a Muslim corps member facing major decisions — career, relationships, financial choices, community initiatives — consultation with knowledgeable, wise, and sincere advisors before deciding is both Sunnah and practically sound.
thursday.extra_notes:
Conditions for effective shura:
1. Consult those with knowledge of the subject matter
2. Consult those who are sincere (not those who will just tell you what you want to hear)
3. Consult those who are pious and fear Allah
4. After receiving advice and performing Istikhara: make a decision and proceed with tawakkul
5. If the consultants disagree: weigh their reasoning, not just their seniority
thursday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 3:159; Al-Ahkam as-Sultaniyyah by al-Mawardi; Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli

friday.title: Jumu'ah as Community Building — The Social Function of Friday Prayer
friday.arabic_text: حَقٌّ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ أَنْ يَغْتَسِلَ فِي كُلِّ سَبْعَةِ أَيَّامٍ يَوْمًا
friday.english_text: It is a right upon every Muslim to bathe once every seven days — on a day.
friday.lesson:
Beyond its spiritual dimensions, Jumu'ah serves a vital social function: bringing the Muslim community together weekly, enabling consultation, solidarity, and information sharing. The Prophet's mosque in Madinah served as a community center, court, meeting hall, and school — all centered around the Jumu'ah prayer.

For Muslim corps members: use Jumu'ah day as a community-building opportunity. Meet with MCAN members, check on fellow Muslims in your area, share knowledge, discuss challenges, and organize support. The masjid is your community center every Friday.
friday.extra_notes:
Ideas for MCAN corps members on Fridays:
- Organize pre-Jumu'ah Islamic study circles
- Hold post-Jumu'ah community meetings
- Arrange visits to Muslim corps members who are sick or struggling
- Coordinate Islamic community development activities
- Maintain a WhatsApp group for Islamic reminders and needs-sharing among Muslim corps members in your LGA
friday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 898; Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah

friday.title: Friday Azkar — The Final Hour Du'a Checklist
friday.arabic_text: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً
friday.english_text: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us. Grant us mercy from Yourself. (Quran 3:8)
friday.transliteration: Rabbana la tuzigh qulubana ba'da idh hadaytana wa hab lana min ladunka rahmah.
friday.benefits: This Quranic du'a of the 'people of knowledge' (Quran 3:7) asks for the greatest of all gifts: protection of guidance after it has been given. The scholars say losing guidance after having had it is among the worst fates — and this du'a is the protection against it. In the Friday hour, ask Allah to keep your heart firm on the right path for the entire service year.
friday.source: Quran 3:8; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Al Imran; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

saturday.title: Amr ibn al-As (RA) — The Strategist Who Found Islam
saturday.arabic_text: أَسْلِمْ تَسْلَمْ يَجْعَلِ اللَّهُ لَكَ مَا قَبْلَهُ
saturday.english_text: Embrace Islam and be safe; Allah will place before you what came before it.
saturday.lesson:
Amr ibn al-As (RA) was one of the sharpest political and military strategists of the Arabian Peninsula — and before his conversion, one of the Prophet's most formidable opponents. After a long search that took him to the court of the Negus in Abyssinia, he embraced Islam on his return journey in 8 AH.

He later led the conquest of Egypt with 4,000 fighters against a vastly larger force — and succeeded. He became the governor of Egypt and used his extraordinary administrative and military intelligence entirely in the service of Islam.

Lesson: The skills you have developed in your field of study — engineering, law, medicine, communication, management — are the same skills Allah may use to advance His religion. The conversion of capability into service for Islam is the transformation of Amr ibn al-As.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 4357; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi; Al-Bidayah wan-Nihayah by Ibn Kathir

saturday.title: Nusaybah bint Ka'b (Umm Umarah) (RA) — The Shield of the Prophet at Uhud
saturday.arabic_text: مَا الْتَفَتُّ يَمِينًا وَلَا شِمَالًا إِلَّا وَأَنَا أَرَاهَا تُقَاتِلُ دُونِي
saturday.english_text: I did not look to my right or my left except that I saw her fighting in my defense.
saturday.lesson:
Nusaybah bint Ka'b (RA), also known as Umm Umarah, was an Ansari woman who participated in multiple battles alongside the Prophet. At Uhud, when many companions fled after the tide turned, Umm Umarah stood firm beside the Prophet — fighting off attackers with a sword and bow, sustaining twelve wounds. The Prophet testified about her: 'Whenever I look right or left, I see her fighting for me.'

She later fought in Yamama and lost her hand in battle — and continued as a courageous member of the Muslim community until her death.

Lesson: The Muslim woman's courage and contribution to the community is not a modern aspiration — it is a well-documented historical reality. Umm Umarah gave more to Islam in one day at Uhud than most men give in a lifetime.
saturday.source: Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar; Usud al-Ghabah by Ibn al-Athir; As-Seerah an-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: Isma'il (AS) — The Ultimate Act of Obedience
sunday.arabic_text: فَلَمَّا أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ
sunday.english_text: And when they had both submitted and he laid him down upon his forehead. (Quran 37:103)
sunday.lesson:
Ibrahim (AS) saw in a dream that he was sacrificing his son Isma'il. He told Isma'il, who said: 'O my father, do what you have been commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient.' When Ibrahim placed his son forehead-first on the ground to carry out the command, Allah called out: 'O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the vision' — and replaced Isma'il with a great ram.

This is the ultimate model of tawakkul: a father and son together, submitting entirely to Allah's command. No argument, no delay, no negotiation — pure trust. This event is commemorated every year at Eid al-Adha and in every sacrifice made in the name of Allah.
sunday.source: Quran 37:99-111; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah as-Saffat; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: Zakariyyah (AS) — Making Du'a in Old Age
sunday.arabic_text: رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِي فَرْدًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الْوَارِثِينَ
sunday.english_text: My Lord, do not leave me alone, and You are the best of inheritors. (Quran 21:89)
sunday.lesson:
Zakariyyah (AS) was an elderly prophet whose wife was barren. Despite old age and physical impossibility, he made du'a to Allah for a righteous heir — not for personal glory but to continue the chain of prophethood and worship in his family. Allah responded with the miraculous birth of Yahya (John the Baptist, AS).

Zakariyyah's story contains a profound principle: du'a is never inappropriate, regardless of how impossible the outcome seems. The Muslim corps member who desires a righteous spouse, righteous children, a good career outcome, or any other 'impossible' thing — make du'a with the same sincere hope Zakariyyah had at an age when human possibility had clearly ended.
sunday.source: Quran 21:89-90; Quran 19:2-11; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah Maryam; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

tuesday.title: Azkar — Du'a for consistency
tuesday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْهُدَى وَالتُّقَى وَالْعَفَافَ وَالْغِنَى
tuesday.english_text: O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity, and self-sufficiency.
tuesday.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'alukal-huda wat-tuqa wal-'afafa wal-ghina.
tuesday.benefits: This comprehensive du'a — related to this week's theme of Azkar — Du'a for consistency — covers four of the most essential gifts: guidance (huda) to the right path, taqwa (God-consciousness) to stay on it, 'afaf (chastity and restraint) from what harms you, and ghina (self-sufficiency) from depending on others for what Allah can provide. When we know Allah's name that is most relevant to our current condition and call on Him by it, our du'a is more sincere and our trust is more grounded. friday.title: Jumu'ah — Consistency Through the Year
friday.arabic_text: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَاةِ مِن يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فَاسْعَوْا إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ
friday.english_text: O you who have believed, when the call to prayer is made on the day of Jumu'ah, proceed to the remembrance of Allah. (Quran 62:9)
friday.lesson: This Friday's theme — Jumu'ah — Consistency Through the Year — is a reminder that Jumu'ah is not only a prayer but a weekly spiritual summit. Every Friday is an opportunity to reset, renew intention, seek forgiveness, make du'a in the blessed hour, and return to the week strengthened. Make the most of this Friday.
friday.extra_notes:
This week's Jumu'ah action plan:
1. Perform ghusl in the morning
2. Read Surah al-Kahf before the prayer
3. Go to the masjid early
4. Make abundant salawat on the Prophet
5. In the final hour before Maghrib: make du'a for yourself, your family, and the Muslim Ummah
6. Pray four rak'ahs of nafl after Jumu'ah
friday.source: Quran 62:9; Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 881; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Friday

saturday.title: Companion: Al-Hasan al-Basri (Tabi'i Scholar)
saturday.arabic_text: كُنَّا نُعَدُّ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ
saturday.english_text: We were counted among the companions of the Messenger of Allah.
saturday.lesson: This week's companion story — Companion: Al-Hasan al-Basri (Tabi'i Scholar) — demonstrates the transformative power of proximity to the Prophet and sincere faith. Each companion embodied a unique aspect of Islamic excellence. Study their lives not as historical curiosities but as living templates. Ask: which aspect of this companion's character do I most need to develop in my current circumstances as a corps member?
saturday.source: As-Seerah an-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi; Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar

saturday.title: Companion Study Week 40 — Continued
saturday.arabic_text: إِنَّ خِيَارَكُمْ أَحَاسِنُكُمْ أَخْلَاقًا
saturday.english_text: The best among you are those with the best character.
saturday.lesson:
As we continue the story of Companion: Al-Hasan al-Basri (Tabi'i Scholar), we see that Islamic excellence is not a single formula but manifested differently in each individual. The companion's response to hardship, their generosity, their knowledge, their courage — these varied enormously, yet each was beloved to the Prophet.

For the corps member: your service year is your opportunity to develop YOUR unique Islamic excellence. What combination of qualities — knowledge, courage, generosity, patience, wisdom — is Allah calling you to develop this year?
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3559; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Good Character

sunday.title: Quran — Surah al-A'la: The Reminder

sunday.english_text: Indeed in that is a sign for people who give thought. (Quran 16:11)
sunday.lesson: This week's Quranic story — Quran — Surah al-A'la: The Reminder — is preserved in the Quran not as historical information but as a timeless lesson. Take time this Sunday to genuinely reflect: what does this story tell me about my current situation, my relationship with Allah, and my responsibilities as a Muslim corps member?
sunday.source: Referenced Quranic surah; Tafsir Ibn Kathir; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir; Tafsir as-Sa'di

sunday.title: Quranic Reflection Week 40 — Application
sunday.arabic_text: أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ
sunday.english_text: Will they not ponder the Quran? (Quran 4:82)
sunday.lesson:
Tadabbur (deep reflection on the Quran) is not the exclusive domain of scholars — it is a command to every Muslim. This week, read the passage related to Quran — Surah al-A'la: The Reminder in your own Quran with full attention. Note:
1. What does this passage tell me about Allah?
2. What does it tell me about human nature?
3. What does it tell me about what I should do differently?
4. What du'a does it inspire in me?

Jot your reflections in a notebook — this is Islamic journaling in the prophetic tradition of tadabbur.
sunday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (relevant surah); Tafsir as-Sa'di (relevant surah); Al-Fawa'id by Ibn al-Qayyim (on Quranic reflection)

sunday.title: Quranic Reflection Week 45 — Application
sunday.arabic_text: أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ
sunday.english_text: Will they not ponder the Quran? (Quran 4:82)
sunday.lesson:
Tadabbur (deep reflection on the Quran) is not the exclusive domain of scholars — it is a command to every Muslim. This week, read the passage related to Quran — Surah al-'Alaq: The First Revelation in your own Quran with full attention. Note:
1. What does this passage tell me about Allah?
2. What does it tell me about human nature?
3. What does it tell me about what I should do differently?
4. What du'a does it inspire in me?

Jot your reflections in a notebook — this is Islamic journaling in the prophetic tradition of tadabbur.

tuesday.english_text: O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity, and self-sufficiency.
tuesday.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'alukal-huda wat-tuqa wal-'afafa wal-ghina.

monday.title: Hadith on Truthfulness in Trade
monday.arabic_text: الْبَيِّعَانِ بِالْخِيَارِ مَا لَمْ يَتَفَرَّقَا، فَإِنْ صَدَقَا وَبَيَّنَا بُورِكَ لَهُمَا فِي بَيْعِهِمَا
monday.english_text: The two parties in a transaction have the right to cancel it as long as they have not separated. If they are honest and make things clear, their transaction will be blessed.
monday.transliteration: Al-bayyi'ani bil-khiyari ma lam yatafarraqa, fa-in sadaqa wa bayyina buraka lahuma fi bay'ihima.
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Hakim ibn Hizam (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (2079) and Sahih Muslim (1532).
monday.lesson: Honesty in commercial transactions earns divine blessing on the deal. Dishonesty — concealing defects, inflating prices, making false claims — removes the barakah. A corps member who is honest in every financial dealing, even small ones, is planting barakah in their livelihood.
monday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 2079; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 1532; Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq

monday.title: Hadith on the Prohibition of Pride
monday.arabic_text: لَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ مَنْ كَانَ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ مِنْ كِبْرٍ
monday.english_text: Whoever has an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart will not enter Paradise.
monday.transliteration: La yadkhulul-jannata man kana fi qalbihi mithqalu dharratin min kibr.
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih Muslim (91).
monday.lesson: Pride (kibr) is defined in the same hadith as 'rejecting truth and looking down on people.' The corps member who dismisses the knowledge of a community elder, who treats support staff with contempt, or who refuses correction — carries the seed of kibr. The cure: remember that you were created from clay and will return to earth.
monday.source: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 91; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Pride; Al-Fawa'id by Ibn al-Qayyim

tuesday.title: Dhikr of Tasbih — SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi 100x
tuesday.arabic_text: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
tuesday.english_text: Glory be to Allah and all praise is due to Him.
tuesday.transliteration: SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi.
tuesday.benefits: Whoever says this 100 times a day will have his sins forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea. (Sahih al-Bukhari 6405). It is also the phrase most beloved to Allah after La ilaha illallah. This single dhikr — 100 times daily — takes approximately two minutes and earns forgiveness of an ocean of sins.
tuesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6405; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2692; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

tuesday.title: Du'a for Rain — Allahumma asqina
tuesday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ أَسْقِنَا غَيْثًا مُغِيثًا مَرِيئًا مَرِيعًا نَافِعًا غَيْرَ ضَارٍّ عَاجِلًا غَيْرَ آجِلٍ
tuesday.english_text: O Allah, send us rain that is helpful, pleasant, fertile, beneficial not harmful, swift not delayed.
tuesday.transliteration: Allahumma asqina ghaythan mugheethan mariyyan maree'an nafi'an ghayra darrin 'ajilan ghayra ajil.
tuesday.benefits: This is the du'a for rain from the authentic Sunnah. For corps members posted in areas experiencing drought, agricultural failure, or water shortage — making this du'a collectively in your community is an act of worship and a means of relief. The Prophet made public du'a for rain (Salat al-Istisqa') in congregation, but individual du'a for rain is always permissible.
tuesday.source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 1169; Al-Adab al-Mufrad by Imam al-Bukhari; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

wednesday.title: Al-Istidraj — Allah's Gradual Allowance of Transgression
wednesday.arabic_text: فَلَمَّا نَسُوا مَا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَبْوَابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ
wednesday.english_text: And when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened to them the doors of every pleasant thing. (Quran 6:44)
wednesday.lesson:
Istidraj is one of the most frightening concepts in Islamic theology: Allah gradually grants worldly blessings to those who persist in sin and disobedience — not as a reward, but as rope that leads them deeper into destruction before sudden punishment. The sign that a blessing is Istidraj: receiving more while growing more distant from Allah.

The test for corps members: When you receive success, promotion, or recognition — does it draw you closer to Allah or further? Success that increases your reliance on Allah is a true blessing. Success that increases your arrogance and distance from Allah is a warning sign.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: How do I distinguish between a real blessing and Istidraj?
A: Ibn al-Qayyim said: 'Look at your heart when the blessing arrives. If it drew you closer to Allah, it is a blessing. If it pulled you further, it is Istidraj.' The antidote is immediate shukr (gratitude) and increased worship upon receiving any blessing.
wednesday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 6:44; Al-Fawa'id by Ibn al-Qayyim; Madarij as-Salikin by Ibn al-Qayyim

wednesday.title: The Barzakh — Life Between Death and Resurrection
wednesday.arabic_text: وَمِن وَرَائِهِم بَرْزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
wednesday.english_text: And behind them is a barrier (Barzakh) until the Day they are resurrected. (Quran 23:100)
wednesday.lesson:
The Barzakh is the period between death and resurrection — a realm that exists beyond human perception but is described in authentic hadith. In the grave: the angels Munkar and Nakir question the deceased about their Lord, religion, and prophet. The righteous experience comfort and see their place in Jannah. The wrongdoers experience constriction and see their place in Jahannam.

For the living: the reality of the Barzakh makes every day of life precious — we do not know when we will cross into it. The Muslim who remembers the grave remembers accountability.
wednesday.extra_notes: Prescribed du'a when passing a graveyard: 'As-salamu 'alaykum ya ahl ad-diyar minal-mu'mineena wal-muslimeen, wa inna in sha'Allah bikum lahiqoon, yas'alullaha lana wa lakumul-'afiyah.' — Peace be upon you, O inhabitants of the dwellings from among the believers and Muslims. We will indeed join you if Allah wills. I ask Allah for well-being for us and for you. (Sahih Muslim 975)
wednesday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 23:100; Kitab ar-Ruh by Ibn al-Qayyim; Ahwal al-Qabr by Ibn Abi al-Dunya

thursday.title: Fiqh of Backbiting and Its Expiation
thursday.arabic_text: وَلَا يَغْتَب بَّعْضُكُم بَعْضًا أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتًا
thursday.english_text: And do not backbite one another. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? (Quran 49:12)
thursday.lesson:
Ghibah (backbiting) is one of the most widespread yet underestimated major sins. The Quran uses the graphic metaphor of eating a dead brother's flesh to convey its severity. The expiation for backbiting requires: stopping the backbiting, sincerely regretting it, making istighfar, and — if possible — seeking forgiveness from the person backbitten. Scholars differ on the last: some say seeking forgiveness is required; others say if telling the person would cause more harm, make du'a for them instead.

For corps members: the shared living and working environment creates abundant opportunities for ghibah. Guard your tongue especially in group chats and casual conversations.
thursday.extra_notes:
What is NOT ghibah (permissible mentions):
- Warning someone about a person's known bad character for their protection
- Complaining to an authority to get redress for wrong done to you
- Mentioning known public sinners in the context of warning others
- Identifying a narrator of hadith when discussing his reliability (jarh wa ta'dil)
thursday.source: Quran 49:12; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-Hujurat; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Backbiting; Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli

thursday.title: Fiqh of Sadaqah al-Fitr — Mandatory End-of-Ramadan Charity
thursday.arabic_text: فَرَضَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ زَكَاةَ الْفِطْرِ طُهْرَةً لِلصَّائِمِ مِنَ اللَّغْوِ وَالرَّفَثِ
thursday.english_text: The Messenger of Allah made Zakat al-Fitr obligatory as a purification of the fasting person from idle and indecent speech.
thursday.lesson:
Sadaqah al-Fitr (Zakat al-Fitr) is wajib on every Muslim who possesses more than their basic needs at the end of Ramadan — for themselves and every dependent. The amount: one sa' (approximately 2.5–3 kg) of staple food (rice, dates, wheat, etc.) per person, or its monetary equivalent according to contemporary scholars. It must be given before the Eid prayer to be valid Zakat al-Fitr; after Eid it becomes ordinary sadaqah.

For corps members: Even on a modest allowance, you likely qualify as able to give Sadaqah al-Fitr. It is one of the most accessible obligatory acts of the year.
thursday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 1503; Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 1609; Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli

friday.title: The Miswak on Friday — Comprehensive Oral Hygiene Sunnah
friday.arabic_text: لَوْلَا أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَى أُمَّتِي لَأَمَرْتُهُمْ بِالسِّوَاكِ مَعَ كُلِّ وُضُوءٍ
friday.english_text: Were it not that I would be causing difficulty for my Ummah, I would have commanded them to use the miswak with every wudu.
friday.lesson: The miswak (tooth-stick from the Arak tree or similar) is one of the most emphasized Sunnahs of personal hygiene. It cleans the mouth, pleases Allah, and was used by the Prophet at every wudu and before prayer. On Friday especially — before the Jumu'ah prayer — using the miswak is both a Sunnah and a means of maximizing the reward of Friday. If miswak is unavailable, using a toothbrush serves the purpose according to most contemporary scholars.
friday.extra_notes:
When to use miswak:
- Before every Salah
- Before every wudu
- Before reciting Quran
- Upon waking from sleep
- Before entering the masjid
- Especially on Friday before Jumu'ah

The Prophet said prayer with miswak is 70 times better than prayer without it (Sunan al-Bayhaqi, al-Albani: Sahih).
friday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 887; Sunan Abi Dawud, Hadith 46; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on Miswak

friday.title: Friday Azkar — Du'a for a Blessed End
friday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْ خَيْرَ عُمُرِي آخِرَهُ وَخَيْرَ عَمَلِي خَوَاتِيمَهُ وَخَيْرَ أَيَّامِي يَوْمَ أَلْقَاكَ
friday.english_text: O Allah, make the best of my life its final part, the best of my deeds their final acts, and the best of my days the day I meet You.
friday.transliteration: Allahumma-j'al khayra 'umuri akhirah, wa khayra 'amali khawatimah, wa khayra ayyami yawma alqak.
friday.benefits: This du'a asks for three gifts: a life that gets better with age and wisdom (not declining into sin or regret), deeds that improve consistently so your final acts are your best, and a death that is the best moment of your existence — meeting Allah in a state of grace. On Friday, in the final hour before Maghrib, make this du'a as your service year progresses.
friday.source: Authenticated in Silsilah as-Sahihah by al-Albani (1771); Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani

saturday.title: Nu'man ibn Bashir (RA) — The Hadith of Halal and Haram
saturday.arabic_text: الْحَلَالُ بَيِّنٌ، وَالْحَرَامُ بَيِّنٌ، وَبَيْنَهُمَا مُشَبَّهَاتٌ
saturday.english_text: The halal is clear, the haram is clear, and between them are doubtful matters.
saturday.lesson:
Nu'man ibn Bashir (RA) was one of the last companions to die, narrating this foundational hadith of Islamic ethics which the scholars consider one of the four hadiths that Islam revolves around. Born in Madinah to an Ansari family, he grew up in the direct company of the Prophet.

His narration of this hadith — describing the analogy of a shepherd grazing around a protected pasture — gave the Muslim world one of its most practical ethical principles: 'Whoever falls into doubtful matters falls into the forbidden, as a shepherd who grazes near a protected pasture is likely to enter it.'

Lesson: The grey area is the danger zone. The Muslim corps member who regularly operates in ambiguous ethical situations — 'it's not exactly haram but...' — is gradually drifting toward the haram. Move away from the grey toward the clear.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 52; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 1599; Jami' al-Ulum wal-Hikam by Ibn Rajab, Hadith 6

saturday.title: Ruqayyah bint Muhammad (RA) — Love and Loss in the Way of Allah
saturday.arabic_text: انْطَلِقَا إِلَى أَرْضٍ تَسِيرُ فِيهَا
saturday.english_text: Go forth to a land where you will travel in it.
saturday.lesson:
Ruqayyah (RA) was the second daughter of the Prophet and Khadijah (RA). She was initially engaged to Utbah ibn Abi Lahab — but after the revelation of Surah al-Masad condemning her father-in-law Abu Lahab, Utbah's family forced him to divorce her. She married Uthman ibn Affan and emigrated with him to Abyssinia — the first Muslim couple to make hijrah.

She and Uthman emigrated twice — to Abyssinia and then to Madinah. She fell seriously ill during the Battle of Badr and died while the battle was being fought. The Prophet's face showed deep grief at her death.

Lesson: The path of the believer is sometimes marked by loss, upheaval, and displacement. Ruqayyah emigrated twice and died young — yet her story is one of dignity, loyalty, and faith in every circumstance.
saturday.source: As-Seerah an-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham; Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi

sunday.title: The Story of the Two Sons of Adam — The First Murder
sunday.arabic_text: مَن قَتَلَ نَفْسًا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا
sunday.english_text: Whoever kills a soul — unless for a soul or for spreading corruption on earth — it is as if he has killed all of mankind. (Quran 5:32)
sunday.lesson:
The story of Qabil (Cain) and Habil (Abel) — the sons of Adam — is the Quran's account of the first murder in human history. Qabil killed his brother out of jealousy over a rejected sacrifice. After the killing, he did not know what to do with the body — until a crow showed him by burying another crow. He buried his brother, then felt remorse.

The Quran draws from this story the absolute sanctity of human life: killing one person is like killing all of humanity. For Muslim corps members working in communities affected by violence, ethnic tension, or sectarian conflict: the Islamic position could not be clearer — human life is sacred.
sunday.source: Quran 5:27-32; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-Ma'idah; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

sunday.title: Adam and Hawwa (AS) — The First Tawbah
sunday.arabic_text: رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أَنفُسَنَا وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ
sunday.english_text: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers. (Quran 7:23)
sunday.lesson:
When Adam and Hawwa (AS) ate from the forbidden tree and were descended to the earth, their first act was this du'a of tawbah. It contains perfect humility: they did not blame the Shaytan (though he had deceived them), they did not minimize their fault, they did not despair of Allah's mercy — they acknowledged their wrong directly and appealed to His forgiveness and mercy.

This is the model of tawbah for every Muslim: own the mistake completely, appeal to Allah's mercy with genuine hope, and move forward. No blame-shifting, no despair.
sunday.source: Quran 7:19-27; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-A'raf; Stories of the Prophets by Ibn Kathir

monday.title: Hadith on the Tongue and Salvation
monday.arabic_text: مَنْ يَضْمَنْ لِي مَا بَيْنَ لَحْيَيْهِ وَمَا بَيْنَ رِجْلَيْهِ أَضْمَنْ لَهُ الْجَنَّةَ
monday.english_text: Whoever guarantees for me what is between his jaws and what is between his legs, I will guarantee him Paradise.
monday.transliteration: Man yadmanu li ma bayna lahyayhi wa ma bayna rijlayhi adman lahul-jannah.
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Sahl ibn Sa'd (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (6474).
monday.lesson: Two organs destroy more people than any others: the tongue and the private parts. Controlling speech — no lying, no backbiting, no slander, no insults — and controlling sexual conduct — no zina, no inappropriate relationships — are the keys to Jannah according to this hadith. Both become especially challenging in the mixed social environment of NYSC. This is the Prophet's direct guarantee.
monday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6474; Riyad as-Salihin, Chapter on the Tongue; Jami' al-Ulum wal-Hikam by Ibn Rajab

monday.title: Hadith on the Sanctity of the Believer
monday.arabic_text: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
monday.english_text: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.
monday.transliteration: Al-muslimu man salimal-muslimuna min lisanihi wa yadih.
monday.reported_by: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with him). Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (10) and Sahih Muslim (40).
monday.lesson: The Prophet defined the Muslim not only by what they believe or perform in worship — but by what they do NOT do to other Muslims: harm them with tongue or hand. By this definition, the most committed 'worshipper' who harms others with words or actions is failing a core test of Islam. True Muslim character is measured by your effect on those around you.
monday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 10; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 40; Jami' al-Ulum wal-Hikam by Ibn Rajab

tuesday.title: Evening Dhikr — Bismika Allahumma amutu
tuesday.arabic_text: بِسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ أَمُوتُ وَأَحْيَا
tuesday.english_text: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.
tuesday.transliteration: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya.
tuesday.benefits: This is the du'a before sleeping — acknowledging that sleep is a form of death and waking is a form of resurrection, all by Allah's name. The Prophet said: 'When you lie down to sleep, say: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya. And when you wake say: Alhamdulillahilladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur.' This pair of du'as brackets sleep with complete consciousness of Allah's sovereignty over life.
tuesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 6314; Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id al-Qahtani; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

tuesday.title: Dhikr for Strength — La hawla wa la quwwata
tuesday.arabic_text: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
tuesday.english_text: There is no power or strength except with Allah.
tuesday.transliteration: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.
tuesday.benefits: This phrase is called a 'treasure from the treasures of Paradise' by the Prophet (Sahih al-Bukhari 4205). It acknowledges complete dependence on Allah for every movement and every act of strength. The scholars say it is especially powerful when facing a task that feels beyond your capacity — it transfers the burden from 'I must do this' to 'Allah, I need Your power to do this.' Say it frequently during challenging workdays.
tuesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 4205; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2704; al-Adhkar by Imam an-Nawawi

wednesday.title: Husn adh-Dhann — Good Assumption About Allah
wednesday.english_text: I am as My servant thinks of Me.
wednesday.lesson:
This hadith qudsi (divine hadith) is one of the most profound in all of Islam. Allah is — with each servant — exactly what that servant believes He is. The believer who thinks well of Allah (husn adh-dhann) receives well. The believer who despairs, doubts Allah's mercy, or assumes Allah will reject them — receives accordingly.

Ibn al-Qayyim said: 'Husn adh-dhann about Allah means that you believe He will have mercy on you, forgive you, relieve your distress, and give you what you asked for.' This is not wishful thinking — it is theological confidence based on knowledge of Allah's attributes.

For corps members: when making du'a, when facing hardship, when waiting for Allah's response — think well of Allah. He is as you expect Him to be.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: Does this mean I should assume Allah will forgive me even if I keep sinning?
A: No. Ibn al-Qayyim distinguishes: husn adh-dhann is the expectation of Allah's mercy COMBINED with sincere tawbah and effort. Assuming forgiveness while continuing in sin is ghurur (delusion), not husn adh-dhann. The believer has good hope in Allah AND fear of falling short.
wednesday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 7405; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2675; Madarij as-Salikin by Ibn al-Qayyim

wednesday.title: Al-Yaqin — Certainty as the Foundation of Action
wednesday.english_text: And worship your Lord until certainty (death) comes to you. (Quran 15:99)
wednesday.lesson:
Yaqin (certainty) is the highest degree of belief — beyond ilm (knowledge) and beyond zann (probability). The Quran's command to worship until 'al-yaqin' refers to death itself being the certainty that ends the obligation of worship. But scholars also interpret it as: worship with yaqin — with absolute certainty in what you are worshipping for and Who you are worshipping.

The believer of high yaqin is not shaken by doubts, is not paralyzed by uncertainty in life's challenges, and worships with full conviction rather than habit. Yaqin is built through: study of the Quran and Sunnah, reflection on Allah's creation, righteous company, and consistent worship.
wednesday.extra_notes:
Q: What should I do when I have doubts about my faith?
A: Doubts are whispers of Shaytan — not a sign of disbelief. The Prophet said: 'This is clear faith' when told of companions feeling troubled by doubts they dare not voice. (Sahih Muslim 132). Seek knowledge to answer the doubt, seek righteous company, increase worship, and make du'a. Do not act on the doubt until you have knowledge.
wednesday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 15:99; Madarij as-Salikin by Ibn al-Qayyim; Kitab al-Iman by Ibn Mandah

thursday.title: Fiqh of Repentance from Zina — Seeking Purity
thursday.arabic_text: وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا الزِّنَىٰ إِنَّهُ كَانَ فَاحِشَةً وَسَاءَ سَبِيلًا
thursday.english_text: And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and is evil as a way. (Quran 17:32)
thursday.lesson:
Zina (unlawful sexual relations) is a major sin described as fasihah (immorality) in the Quran. The prohibition covers all steps leading to it: free mixing, seclusion with a non-mahram, flirtatious speech, and pornography — not just the act itself. This is why the Quran says 'do not approach' (la taqrabu) rather than 'do not do.'

For corps members in mixed environments: prevention is through lowering the gaze, avoiding seclusion, maintaining Islamic dress, filling time with productive worship, and remembering that Shaytan works gradually — from the first look to the final act.
thursday.extra_notes: For those who have fallen into this sin: the door of tawbah is open. The conditions of tawbah (stopping, remorse, firm resolve) apply. The person does not need to confess to any human authority — they confess only to Allah. Many of the greatest companions of the Prophet had committed serious sins before Islam and were forgiven completely. The mercy of Allah is unlimited for sincere tawbah.
thursday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Quran 17:32; Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli; Halal and Haram in Islam by Yusuf al-Qaradawi

thursday.title: Fiqh of Sihr and Its Islamic Ruling
thursday.arabic_text: وَاتَّبَعُوا مَا تَتْلُو الشَّيَاطِينُ عَلَىٰ مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَانَ وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَانُ وَلَٰكِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ كَفَرُوا
thursday.english_text: And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Sulayman. It was not Sulayman who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved. (Quran 2:102)
thursday.lesson:
Sihr (magic/sorcery) is real according to the Quran and Sunnah — and practicing or seeking it is a major sin, potentially constituting kufr. The Prophet was affected by sihr once (the famous case of Labid ibn al-A'sam) and cured by Quranic recitation and du'a. The correct Islamic response to sihr: ruqyah shariyyah (Quranic healing), seeking refuge in the Quran, and avoiding all contact with practitioners of magic.

For corps members posted in communities where traditional magic, juju, or herbalist practices are common: participating in or supporting these practices is haram. Seeking protection through Islamic means is not only sufficient but superior.
thursday.extra_notes:
Protection from sihr and evil eye:
1. Recite Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer and before sleep
2. Recite the last two verses of Surah al-Baqarah every night
3. Recite the three Quls morning and evening
4. Say 'Bismillah' before all important actions
5. Avoid showing off blessings unnecessarily (nazar awareness)
thursday.source: Quran 2:102; Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 5765 (case of Prophet and sihr); Al-Fiqh al-Islami wa Adillatuh by Wahbah az-Zuhayli

friday.title: Attending Jumu'ah in Difficult Weather or Circumstances
friday.arabic_text: إِذَا ابْتَلَّتِ النِّعَالُ فَالصَّلَاةُ فِي الرِّحَالِ
friday.english_text: When the sandals get wet (from rain), the prayer may be in the dwellings (homes).
friday.lesson:
The Sunnah provides dispensation for missing congregational prayer (and in the Hanbali school, Jumu'ah) in cases of severe rain, mud, extreme cold, illness, or compelling necessity. This demonstrates Islam's balance: establishing the prayer is obligatory, but Allah does not intend hardship.

However, this dispensation is for genuine difficulty — not convenience. A corps member who skips Jumu'ah because of light rain, mild tiredness, or a TV program is misusing the dispensation. The Sunnah is clear: when you CAN attend, attend. When you genuinely CANNOT, perform Dhuhr and seek forgiveness.
friday.extra_notes:
What to do when Jumu'ah is genuinely inaccessible:
1. Perform Dhuhr prayer in full (4 rak'ahs)
2. Make the intention of Dhuhr, not Jumu'ah
3. Make sincere du'a for the ability to attend the next Jumu'ah
4. Do not treat this as a permanent solution — always seek to establish Jumu'ah attendance
friday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 901; Fiqh us-Sunnah by Sayyid Sabiq; Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah

friday.title: Friday Azkar — Du'a for the Youth of Islam
friday.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ أَصْلِحْ شَبَابَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَثَبِّتْهُمْ عَلَى دِينِكَ
friday.english_text: O Allah, reform the youth of the Muslims and keep them firm upon Your religion.
friday.transliteration: Allahumma aslih shababal-muslimeen wa thabbit-hum 'ala deenik.
friday.benefits: On Friday, from the most blessed hour of the most blessed day of the week, the Muslim corps member — themselves a young Muslim — should make du'a for all the young Muslims facing fitna (trial) across the world. This du'a is an act of Muslim brotherhood and a prayer that will return to you, because when you make du'a for your brothers and sisters, an angel says 'and the same for you.' (Sahih Muslim 2732)
friday.source: Inspired by prophetic du'a for the Ummah; authenticated in the collection of scholars; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 2732 (angel's response to du'a for others)

saturday.title: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (RA) — Keeper of the Prophet's Secrets
saturday.arabic_text: كَانَ النَّاسُ يَسْأَلُونَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عَنِ الْخَيْرِ وَكُنْتُ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ الشَّرِّ مَخَافَةَ أَنْ يُدْرِكَنِي
saturday.english_text: People used to ask the Prophet about good, but I used to ask him about evil, fearing it might reach me.
saturday.lesson:
Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (RA) was the companion to whom the Prophet confided the names of the hypocrites of Madinah — making him the keeper of the most sensitive secret in the Muslim community. Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) used to check whether Hudhayfah would pray the janazah over people who died — if Hudhayfah prayed, Umar knew the deceased was not a hypocrite.

Hudhayfah's wisdom in asking about evil rather than good alone shows mature spiritual intelligence: knowing the signs of corruption, hypocrisy, and fitna helps you avoid them. He narrated many hadiths about the end times and the signs of fitnah.

Lesson: Islamic education is incomplete without knowing what to avoid. Learn the signs of hypocrisy, the nature of major sins, and the warnings of the Prophet — so that you can navigate away from them.
saturday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3606; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 1847; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi

saturday.title: Umm al-Fadl Lubaba bint al-Harith (RA) — The Second Woman to Embrace Islam
saturday.arabic_text: كُنَّا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ وَأَنَا فِي الرَّكْبِ
saturday.english_text: We were with the Prophet and I was among the riders.
saturday.lesson:
Umm al-Fadl (RA) is said to be the second woman to embrace Islam after Khadijah. She was the wife of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib (the Prophet's uncle) and the mother of Abdullah ibn Abbas — the great scholar. When Abu Lahab insulted one of the Prophet's companions in her presence, she struck him with a tent pole so hard it left a wound from which he died a week later.

She narrated numerous hadith and was known for her sharp memory and her proximity to the Prophet's family. Her courage in standing up to Abu Lahab in his own home, when the Muslims were in their weakest phase, is a remarkable act of personal bravery.

Lesson: The Muslim woman's courage is not passive. Umm al-Fadl's physical courage, her early faith, and her role in nurturing one of Islam's greatest scholars — all from the domestic sphere — demonstrate that the home is itself a battlefield and a school.
saturday.source: Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar; Siyar A'lam an-Nubala by Imam adh-Dhahabi; Sahih al-Bukhari references

sunday.title: Surah al-Fatiha — The Opening and Its Secrets
sunday.arabic_text: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
sunday.english_text: All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds. (Quran 1:2)
sunday.lesson:
Surah al-Fatiha is recited at minimum 17 times daily in obligatory prayers — yet how many Muslims truly reflect on its meaning? Ibn al-Qayyim devoted an entire book to its secrets. It contains: the three foundations of worship (hamd/praise, rububiyyah/lordship, ubudiyyah/servitude), the two names of mercy (Ar-Rahman, Ar-Raheem), declaration of the Day of Judgment, the essence of du'a (guidance to the straight path), and the three types of people (those Allah blessed, those who earned anger, and those who went astray).

The Prophet called it 'Umm al-Quran' (Mother of the Quran) — because all of Islam's themes are contained within its seven verses. A corps member who reflects on Surah al-Fatiha in every prayer transforms each salah from recitation to a living conversation with Allah.
sunday.source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-Fatiha; Madarij as-Salikin by Ibn al-Qayyim; Al-Fatiha between Praise and Prayer by Ibn al-Qayyim

sunday.title: Surah al-Ikhlas — A Third of the Quran
sunday.arabic_text: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ
sunday.english_text: Say: He is Allah, One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent. (Quran 112:1-4)
sunday.lesson:
Surah al-Ikhlas is described by the Prophet as equivalent to one-third of the Quran (Sahih al-Bukhari 5013) — because the Quran contains three categories: tawheed, stories, and rulings. This surah covers the entire category of Tawheed in four verses. Each verse answers a false claim: (1) Ahad refutes polytheism; (2) as-Samad refutes atheism (He needs nothing and everything needs Him); (3) lam yalid refutes those who call Him 'Father'; (4) walam yulad refutes those who called Him a born being.

For the Muslim corps member in a multi-faith environment: knowing the theological significance of this surah equips you for respectful, clear explanation of Islamic monotheism to any questioner.
sunday.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 5013; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah al-Ikhlas; Al-Fawa'id by Ibn al-Qayyim
